5. References: USP <1072>

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Qualification of EM Incubators
1. Purpose: To ensure incubators used for EM provide accurate and consistent conditions.
2. Scope: All incubators used for microbial growth.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform temperature mapping.
2) Calibrate sensors.
3) Verify uniformity and stability.
4) Document qualification.
5) Schedule requalification annually.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Temperature uniformity ±2 °C; calibration traceable.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Handling of Mixed Flora Plates
1. Purpose: To define approach for interpreting plates with mixed microbial growth.
2. Scope: All EM plates showing multiple colony morphologies.
3. Procedure:
1) Enumerate total CFU.
2) Subculture representative colonies.
3) Identify organisms.
4) Assess significance relative to environment.
5) Document findings.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All morphologies evaluated; identification performed for action-level events.
5. References: USP <1116>

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Documentation of Sampling Deviations
1. Purpose: To ensure deviations from EM procedures are properly recorded and investigated.
2. Scope: All EM activities.
3. Procedure:
1) Record deviation details immediately.
2) Assess impact on data integrity.
3) Initiate deviation investigation.
4) Implement CAPA.
5) Document closure.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Deviations recorded within 1 day; investigation closed within 30 days.
5. References: QC_SOP_010

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Qualification of EM Personnel
1. Purpose: To ensure personnel are competent in EM sampling techniques.
2. Scope: All personnel performing EM.
3. Procedure:
1) Provide theoretical and practical training.
2) Conduct supervised sampling exercises.
3) Evaluate performance through proficiency testing.
4) Document qualification.
5) Requalify annually.
4. Acceptance Criteria: ≥ 90 % proficiency score; no critical errors during assessment.
5. References: QC_SOP_042

Title: Environmental Monitoring – EM Equipment Preventive Maintenance
1. Purpose: To ensure reliability of EM equipment through routine maintenance.
2. Scope: Air samplers, particle counters, incubators.
3. Procedure:
1) Schedule maintenance per manufacturer recommendations.
2) Perform cleaning, calibration, and part replacement.
3) Document maintenance activities.
4) Verify performance post-maintenance.
5) Update equipment logs.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No overdue maintenance; equipment performs within specifications.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Data Backup and Archiving
1. Purpose: To ensure secure storage and retrieval of EM data.
2. Scope: All electronic EM records.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform daily data backup.
2) Store backups in secure servers.
3) Verify backup integrity periodically.
4) Maintain access control.
5) Archive data per retention policy.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Backup frequency ≤ 24 hours; data retrievable within 24 hours.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Integration with Deviation and CAPA Systems
1. Purpose: To ensure EM excursions are linked to deviation and CAPA workflows.
2. Scope: All EM results exceeding limits.
3. Procedure:
1) Initiate deviation record for excursion.
2) Link EM data to CAPA system.
3) Track corrective and preventive actions.
4) Verify effectiveness.
5) Close records.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % linkage of excursions to CAPA; effectiveness verified within 60 days.
5. References: QC_SOP_010

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Qualification of New Cleanroom After Construction
1. Purpose: To verify that newly constructed or renovated cleanrooms meet required environmental classification and control standards prior to operational use.
2. Scope: Applies to all new or modified ISO-classified areas used for manufacturing or QC testing.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform non-viable particle count testing at rest and in operation per ISO 14644-1.
2) Conduct viable air, surface, and personnel monitoring across defined locations.
3) Execute airflow visualization (smoke study) to confirm unidirectional flow in critical zones.
4) Verify HEPA filter integrity using PAO/DOP testing.
5) Compile qualification report and obtain QA approval before release for use.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All ISO classification limits met; HEPA integrity ≤0.01 % penetration; no airflow turbulence in ISO 5 zones.
5. References: ISO 14644-1, EU Annex 1

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Trending of Identified Microflora
1. Purpose: To establish long-term tracking and analysis of identified environmental microorganisms for contamination control.
2. Scope: All identified isolates from EM activities.
3. Procedure:
1) Maintain database of identified organisms with location, date, and count.
2) Classify isolates by genus/species and risk category.
3) Perform periodic trend analysis to detect recurring organisms.
4) Correlate findings with cleaning and disinfection practices.
5) Initiate investigation for persistent or objectionable organisms.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No recurring objectionable organism across three consecutive events; trends reviewed quarterly.
5. References: USP <1116>, QC_SOP_170

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Qualification of New Disinfectants
1. Purpose: To validate efficacy of new disinfectants introduced into cleanroom cleaning programs.
2. Scope: All disinfectants used in classified areas.
3. Procedure:
1) Select representative environmental isolates including bacteria and fungi.
2) Apply disinfectant to inoculated surfaces at defined contact times.
3) Measure microbial reduction using standard plate counts.
4) Compare efficacy against existing disinfectants.
5) Document validation results and approve for use.
4. Acceptance Criteria: ≥3 log reduction for vegetative organisms; ≥2 log reduction for fungi within specified contact time.
5. References: USP <1072>

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Routine Review of EM Alarm Logs
1. Purpose: To ensure timely detection and response to EM system alarms and excursions.
2. Scope: All monitoring systems including particle counters and environmental sensors.
3. Procedure:
1) Review alarm logs daily for temperature, humidity, and particle count excursions.
2) Verify alarm acknowledgement and response actions.
3) Correlate alarms with EM sampling data.
4) Document findings and escalate unresolved alarms.
5) Archive reviewed logs.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All alarms reviewed within 24 hours; no unacknowledged alarms; corrective actions documented.
5. References: QC_SOP_156

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Qualification of Air Samplers
1. Purpose: To ensure air samplers provide accurate and reproducible results.
2. Scope: All active air sampling devices used in EM.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate flow rate using traceable standard.
2) Perform recovery efficiency test using known microbial challenge.
3) Compare results across multiple runs.
4) Document performance qualification.
5) Schedule periodic requalification.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Flow rate accuracy ±5 %; recovery efficiency ≥70 %; consistent performance across three runs.
5. References: ISO 14698

Title: Environmental Monitoring – EM Sampling During Maintenance Activities
1. Purpose: To assess contamination risk during and after maintenance interventions in cleanrooms.
2. Scope: All maintenance activities in classified areas.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform baseline EM before maintenance.
2) Conduct additional sampling during and after maintenance activities.
3) Compare results with baseline data.
4) Evaluate impact on cleanroom classification.
5) Document findings and approve return to operation.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No increase beyond action limits; cleanroom restored to baseline conditions before release.
5. References: EU Annex 1

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Qualification of EM Software Systems
1. Purpose: To ensure EM data management systems meet regulatory requirements for data integrity.
2. Scope: All software systems used for EM data collection and analysis.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform installation, operational, and performance qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ).
2) Verify audit trail functionality and user access controls.
3) Test data backup and recovery procedures.
4) Validate data processing and reporting accuracy.
5) Document validation report.
4. Acceptance Criteria: System compliant with 21 CFR Part 11; audit trails complete; no data loss during testing.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Monitoring of Cleanroom Garments
1. Purpose: To assess microbial contamination on reusable cleanroom garments.
2. Scope: All garments used in ISO-classified areas.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect samples from garments after use using contact plates or swabs.
2) Incubate and enumerate microbial growth.
3) Evaluate cleaning and laundering effectiveness.
4) Trend results over time.
5) Investigate repeated contamination.
4. Acceptance Criteria: ISO 5 ≤1 CFU per sampled area; no increasing contamination trend.
5. References: EU Annex 1

Title: Environmental Monitoring – Periodic Requalification of EM Program
1. Purpose: To ensure continued effectiveness of EM program through periodic requalification.
2. Scope: Entire EM program including sampling plans and limits.
3. Procedure:
1) Review historical EM data and trends.
2) Reassess sampling locations and frequencies.
3) Revalidate alert and action limits.
4) Update documentation.
5) Obtain QA approval.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Requalification completed every 12 months; changes documented and approved.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Environmental Monitoring – EM Program Annual Summary Report
1. Purpose: To compile and evaluate annual EM performance for quality oversight.
2. Scope: All EM data generated within the year.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect all EM data, deviations, and CAPA records.
2) Perform statistical analysis and trend evaluation.
3) Identify recurring issues and improvement areas.
4) Prepare summary report.
5) Review and approve by QA management.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Report completed within 60 days of year-end; all trends and deviations addressed.
5. References: QC_SOP_182

Title: Cleaning Validation – Cleaning Agent Selection and Justification
1. Purpose: To define criteria for selecting appropriate cleaning agents for equipment cleaning validation.
2. Scope: All manufacturing equipment requiring validated cleaning procedures.
3. Procedure:
1) Evaluate solubility of product residues in candidate cleaning agents.
2) Assess compatibility with equipment materials.
3) Review toxicity and environmental impact.
4) Perform laboratory-scale cleaning studies.
5) Document selection rationale.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Cleaning agent removes ≥99.0 % residue; no equipment damage; safety criteria met.
5. References: FDA Cleaning Validation Guidance

Title: Cleaning Validation – Residue Limit Calculation
1. Purpose: To establish acceptable residue limits for cleaning validation.
2. Scope: All products manufactured on shared equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Determine maximum allowable carryover (MACO) based on toxicity or dose.
2) Calculate residue limits using worst-case assumptions.
3) Convert limits to surface area basis.
4) Document calculations.
5) Approve limits.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Limits scientifically justified; calculations verified; safety margin applied.
5. References: PIC/S PI 006

Title: Cleaning Validation – Swab Sampling Technique
1. Purpose: To standardize swab sampling for residue analysis.
2. Scope: All equipment surfaces.
3. Procedure:
1) Use pre-moistened swab.
2) Swab defined area using consistent pattern.
3) Extract residue into solvent.
4) Analyze sample.
5) Record results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Recovery ≥70 %; sampling area within ±10 %.
5. References: QC_SOP_175

Title: Cleaning Validation – Rinse Sampling Procedure
1. Purpose: To assess residue levels using rinse sampling method.
2. Scope: Equipment with complex geometry.
3. Procedure:
1) Rinse equipment with defined volume of solvent.
2) Collect rinse sample.
3) Analyze for residues.
4) Compare with limits.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residue below calculated limit; rinse volume consistent ±5 %.
5. References: PIC/S PI 006

Title: Cleaning Validation – Cleaning Process Qualification
1. Purpose: To validate effectiveness of cleaning process.
2. Scope: All equipment cleaning procedures.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform three consecutive cleaning runs.
2) Collect swab and rinse samples.
3) Analyze for residues.
4) Compare with limits.
5) Document validation report.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All samples below limits; reproducibility demonstrated.
5. References: FDA Guidance

Title: Cleaning Validation – Visual Inspection Criteria
1. Purpose: To define visual cleanliness standards.
2. Scope: All cleaned equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Inspect surfaces under adequate lighting.
2) Check for visible residues.
3) Document findings.
4) Approve or reject equipment.
5) Record inspection.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No visible residue; surface clean and dry.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Cleaning Validation – Worst-Case Product Selection
1. Purpose: To identify worst-case products for validation.
2. Scope: Multi-product facilities.
3. Procedure:
1) Evaluate product toxicity, solubility, and potency.
2) Rank products.
3) Select worst-case.
4) Document rationale.
5) Approve selection.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Selection justified and documented.
5. References: PIC/S PI 006

Title: Cleaning Validation – Cleaning Hold Time Study
1. Purpose: To determine maximum hold time before cleaning.
2. Scope: All equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Allow equipment to sit for defined periods.
2) Perform cleaning.
3) Analyze residues.
4) Compare results.
5) Document findings.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residues below limits at maximum hold time.
5. References: FDA Guidance

Title: Cleaning Validation – Clean Hold Time Study
1. Purpose: To establish maximum hold time after cleaning.
2. Scope: All equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Clean equipment.
2) Store for defined intervals.
3) Sample surfaces.
4) Analyze contamination.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No microbial growth; residue within limits.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Cleaning Validation – Documentation and Reporting
1. Purpose: To ensure proper documentation of cleaning validation.
2. Scope: All validation studies.
3. Procedure:
1) Compile data.
2) Review results.
3) Prepare report.
4) Approve by QA.
5) Archive records.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Complete documentation; QA approval obtained.
5. References: QC_SOP_032

Title: Cleaning Validation – Recovery Study for Swab and Rinse Methods
1. Purpose: To determine the recovery efficiency of sampling methods used in cleaning validation to ensure accurate quantification of residues.
2. Scope: Applies to all swab and rinse sampling techniques used across validated equipment surfaces.
3. Procedure:
1) Spike representative surfaces with known quantity of target residue at relevant concentration levels.
2) Allow residue to dry under controlled conditions simulating worst-case hold time.
3) Perform swab sampling on defined area (e.g., 25 cm²) and/or rinse sampling with validated volume.
4) Analyze samples using validated analytical method (e.g., HPLC-UV).
5) Calculate % recovery by comparing measured vs applied amount and document variability.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Mean recovery ≥ 70.0 % for swab and ≥ 80.0 % for rinse; %RSD ≤ 15.0 % across replicates.
5. References: PIC/S PI 006, QC_SOP_203

Title: Cleaning Validation – Equipment Grouping Strategy
1. Purpose: To justify grouping of similar equipment for cleaning validation to reduce redundant studies.
2. Scope: All manufacturing equipment within same product family and design category.
3. Procedure:
1) Evaluate equipment based on design, material of construction, and cleanability.
2) Identify worst-case equipment within group (e.g., largest surface area, hardest-to-clean geometry).
3) Document grouping rationale including risk assessment and product properties.
4) Validate cleaning process on worst-case equipment.
5) Apply validation to grouped equipment with documented justification.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Grouping scientifically justified; worst-case validation successful; QA approval obtained prior to implementation.
5. References: EU Annex 15, PIC/S PI 006

Title: Cleaning Validation – Analytical Method for Residue Detection
1. Purpose: To define requirements for analytical methods used to detect cleaning residues.
2. Scope: All methods (e.g., HPLC, TOC) used in cleaning validation studies.
3. Procedure:
1) Select method based on residue properties (specific vs non-specific).
2) Validate method for specificity, accuracy, precision, and LOQ in presence of cleaning matrix.
3) Prepare calibration standards and matrix-matched samples.
4) Analyze validation samples and document performance characteristics.
5) Approve method for routine use in cleaning validation.
4. Acceptance Criteria: LOQ ≤ calculated residue limit; recovery 80.0–120.0 %; %RSD ≤ 10.0 % at LOQ.
5. References: ICH Q2(R2), QC_SOP_077

Title: Cleaning Validation – Cleaning Cycle Parameter Verification
1. Purpose: To verify that defined cleaning parameters consistently achieve required cleanliness levels.
2. Scope: Automated and manual cleaning processes for manufacturing equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Define critical parameters such as temperature, contact time, detergent concentration, and flow rate.
2) Execute cleaning cycle using defined parameters on worst-case equipment.
3) Monitor and record parameters throughout cleaning cycle.
4) Collect swab/rinse samples post-cleaning.
5) Analyze results and compare with acceptance limits.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All critical parameters within ±10.0 % of set values; residues below established limits in all replicates.
5. References: FDA Cleaning Validation Guidance

Title: Cleaning Validation – Verification vs Validation Strategy
1. Purpose: To differentiate between routine cleaning verification and initial validation activities.
2. Scope: All cleaning processes in GMP operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform full validation for new equipment or products using three consecutive successful runs.
2) For routine operations, perform periodic verification sampling based on risk.
3) Define frequency and locations for verification sampling.
4) Evaluate results against established limits.
5) Document justification for verification strategy.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Validation requires 3/3 successful runs; verification results within limits ≥ 95.0 % of the time.
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_205

Title: Cleaning Validation – Detergent Residue Analysis
1. Purpose: To ensure removal of cleaning agents from equipment surfaces.
2. Scope: All cleaning processes using detergents or solvents.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify marker compound for detergent (e.g., surfactant).
2) Develop and validate analytical method (e.g., TOC or specific assay).
3) Perform swab/rinse sampling post-cleaning.
4) Analyze samples and quantify detergent residue.
5) Compare with established acceptance criteria.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Detergent residue ≤ 10.0 ppm or as justified toxicologically; %RSD ≤ 15.0 %.
5. References: USP <643>, PIC/S PI 006

Title: Cleaning Validation – Equipment Surface Area Determination
1. Purpose: To calculate total and worst-case surface areas for residue limit conversion.
2. Scope: All equipment included in cleaning validation.
3. Procedure:
1) Obtain engineering drawings and specifications of equipment.
2) Calculate total product-contact surface area.
3) Identify hardest-to-clean locations (e.g., joints, dead legs).
4) Convert MACO to surface area-based limits (µg/cm²).
5) Document calculations and assumptions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Calculations verified by second reviewer; worst-case area identified and justified.
5. References: PIC/S PI 006, QC_SOP_202

Title: Cleaning Validation – Cross-Contamination Risk Assessment
1. Purpose: To assess risk of cross-contamination between products during equipment changeover.
2. Scope: Multi-product manufacturing facilities.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify products manufactured on shared equipment.
2) Evaluate toxicity, potency, and solubility of residues.
3) Calculate potential carryover levels.
4) Compare with acceptable exposure limits.
5) Document risk assessment and mitigation measures.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Risk levels within acceptable limits; mitigation strategies implemented for high-risk products.
5. References: EMA Guideline on Shared Facilities

Title: Cleaning Validation – Verification of Manual Cleaning Techniques
1. Purpose: To ensure manual cleaning procedures are reproducible and effective.
2. Scope: Equipment cleaned manually without automation.
3. Procedure:
1) Train operators on standardized cleaning steps and sequence.
2) Execute manual cleaning on worst-case equipment.
3) Perform swab sampling at predefined locations.
4) Analyze samples for residues.
5) Evaluate variability between operators.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residues below limits; inter-operator %RSD ≤ 20.0 %; no systematic bias observed.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Cleaning Validation – Revalidation Triggers and Requirements
1. Purpose: To define conditions requiring revalidation of cleaning processes.
2. Scope: All validated cleaning procedures.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify triggers such as new product introduction, equipment modification, or cleaning agent change.
2) Assess impact of change on cleaning effectiveness.
3) Perform partial or full revalidation as required.
4) Document rationale and validation results.
5) Obtain QA approval before implementation.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Revalidation completed prior to change implementation; results meet original validation criteria.
5. References: ICH Q10, QC_SOP_099

Title: Cleaning Validation – Documentation of Sampling Locations
1. Purpose: To standardize identification and documentation of sampling sites.
2. Scope: All equipment included in cleaning validation studies.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify worst-case locations based on design and flow patterns.
2) Mark sampling sites on equipment diagrams.
3) Assign unique identifiers to each location.
4) Use consistent sampling areas (e.g., 25 cm²).
5) Record sampling details in validation protocol.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All critical locations sampled; documentation complete and traceable.
5. References: QC_SOP_203

Title: Cleaning Validation – Visual Residue Detection Aids
1. Purpose: To enhance detection of residues using visual aids such as UV light or dyes.
2. Scope: All equipment cleaning processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Apply fluorescent marker or dye to simulate residue.
2) Perform cleaning procedure.
3) Inspect surfaces under UV light.
4) Identify residual contamination areas.
5) Document findings and improve cleaning procedure.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No detectable fluorescence post-cleaning; method validated for sensitivity.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Cleaning Validation – Cleaning Process Robustness Assessment
1. Purpose: To evaluate robustness of cleaning process under variable conditions.
2. Scope: All validated cleaning procedures.
3. Procedure:
1) Vary cleaning parameters within defined ranges (e.g., ±10 % detergent concentration).
2) Perform cleaning runs under varied conditions.
3) Collect and analyze residue samples.
4) Compare results with nominal conditions.
5) Document impact of variations.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residues remain below limits under all tested conditions.
5. References: ICH Q2(R2)

Title: Cleaning Validation – Equipment Cleanability Study
1. Purpose: To assess ease of cleaning for new equipment designs.
2. Scope: New or modified equipment prior to qualification.
3. Procedure:
1) Simulate product contact and residue deposition.
2) Perform standard cleaning procedure.
3) Evaluate residue removal efficiency.
4) Identify areas of poor cleanability.
5) Recommend design improvements if necessary.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residue removal ≥ 99.0 %; no inaccessible areas retaining residue.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Cleaning Validation – Cleaning Logbook Management
1. Purpose: To ensure accurate documentation of cleaning activities.
2. Scope: All equipment cleaning records.
3. Procedure:
1) Record date, time, equipment ID, and cleaning method.
2) Document operator name and signature.
3) Verify completion of cleaning steps.
4) Review logbook entries.
5) Archive records.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No missing entries; entries attributable and legible; reviewed within 24 hours.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Cleaning Validation – Worst-Case Sampling Location Justification
1. Purpose: To define and justify worst-case sampling locations on equipment for effective residue detection during cleaning validation.
2. Scope: All shared manufacturing equipment subject to cleaning validation.
3. Procedure:
1) Review equipment design drawings to identify areas with limited accessibility, dead legs, or complex geometry.
2) Assess product flow paths and residue accumulation likelihood based on prior manufacturing experience.
3) Rank potential locations using risk factors such as surface roughness, exposure time, and cleaning accessibility.
4) Select representative worst-case locations and document rationale with diagrams.
5) Include selected sites in validation protocol and ensure consistent sampling area (e.g., 25 cm²).
4. Acceptance Criteria: All high-risk areas included; rationale documented and approved by QA; locations consistently sampled across runs.
5. References: PIC/S PI 006, QC_SOP_221

Title: Cleaning Validation – Rinse Volume Determination and Control
1. Purpose: To establish and control rinse volumes used for residue recovery during cleaning validation.
2. Scope: Equipment cleaned using rinse sampling approaches.
3. Procedure:
1) Determine minimum rinse volume required to contact all product-contact surfaces.
2) Validate rinse efficiency using spiked recovery studies.
3) Standardize rinse volume and flow rate in cleaning procedures.
4) Collect rinse samples using calibrated containers.
5) Record actual volume used and compare to validated value.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Rinse volume within ±5.0 % of validated volume; recovery ≥ 80.0 %; no pooling observed.
5. References: PIC/S PI 006, QC_SOP_204

Title: Cleaning Validation – Time Between Cleaning and Sampling (Dirty Hold Time)
1. Purpose: To establish maximum allowable time equipment can remain dirty prior to cleaning without impacting cleanability.
2. Scope: All equipment used in batch manufacturing processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Simulate production and allow equipment to remain uncleaned for defined intervals (e.g., 8, 24, 48 hours).
2) Perform validated cleaning procedure at each interval.
3) Collect swab and/or rinse samples at worst-case locations.
4) Analyze for residues using validated method.
5) Compare results across time intervals.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residue levels remain below limits at maximum defined hold time; no visible hard-to-remove deposits.
5. References: FDA Cleaning Validation Guidance, QC_SOP_208

Title: Cleaning Validation – Clean Hold Time Study for Microbial Control
1. Purpose: To determine allowable time equipment can remain clean before use without microbial contamination.
2. Scope: Equipment used for non-sterile and sterile product manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform validated cleaning and drying of equipment.
2) Store equipment under defined environmental conditions.
3) Sample surfaces at intervals (e.g., 24, 48, 72 hours) using swabs.
4) Perform microbial limit testing on samples.
5) Evaluate growth trends and establish maximum hold time.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Total aerobic microbial count ≤ established limits (e.g., ≤ 10 CFU/25 cm²); no objectionable organisms detected.
5. References: EU Annex 15, USP <61>

Title: Cleaning Validation – Detergent Contact Time Optimization
1. Purpose: To determine optimal contact time required for cleaning agent effectiveness.
2. Scope: All cleaning processes using chemical detergents.
3. Procedure:
1) Apply detergent to soiled surfaces under controlled conditions.
2) Vary contact time (e.g., 5, 10, 20 minutes).
3) Perform cleaning and collect residue samples.
4) Analyze samples for residual product and detergent.
5) Identify minimum effective contact time.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residue removal ≥ 99.0 % at defined contact time; detergent residue below acceptance limits.
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_214

Title: Cleaning Validation – Verification of Automated Cleaning Systems (CIP)
1. Purpose: To validate cleaning-in-place (CIP) systems for effectiveness and reproducibility.
2. Scope: All automated cleaning systems used in manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Define CIP cycle parameters including temperature, flow rate, and detergent concentration.
2) Execute three consecutive CIP cycles on worst-case equipment.
3) Collect rinse samples at defined points.
4) Analyze for residues and cleaning agent.
5) Evaluate reproducibility across runs.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All samples below residue limits; cycle parameters within ±10.0 % of set values; reproducible results across runs.
5. References: FDA Cleaning Validation Guidance

Title: Cleaning Validation – Verification of Equipment Drying Effectiveness
1. Purpose: To ensure adequate drying of equipment after cleaning to prevent microbial growth.
2. Scope: All cleaned equipment prior to reuse.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform cleaning followed by drying step using defined method (e.g., air purge).
2) Measure residual moisture using validated technique (e.g., Karl Fischer).
3) Inspect visually for water accumulation.
4) Document drying time and conditions.
5) Verify dryness prior to storage or use.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residual moisture ≤ 0.5 % or as justified; no visible water droplets.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Cleaning Validation – Cleaning Procedure Training and Qualification
1. Purpose: To ensure personnel are adequately trained in cleaning procedures.
2. Scope: All operators performing cleaning activities.
3. Procedure:
1) Provide theoretical training on cleaning principles and SOPs.
2) Conduct supervised practical demonstrations.
3) Evaluate operator performance using test scenarios.
4) Document training completion and competency assessment.
5) Requalify personnel annually.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Training score ≥ 90.0 %; no critical errors during demonstration.
5. References: QC_SOP_042

Title: Cleaning Validation – Visual Cleanliness Inspection Under Enhanced Lighting
1. Purpose: To improve detection of residues through enhanced visual inspection conditions.
2. Scope: All cleaned equipment surfaces.
3. Procedure:
1) Inspect surfaces under high-intensity white light (≥ 1000 lux).
2) Use mirrors or borescopes for hard-to-see areas.
3) Check for residues, streaks, or discoloration.
4) Document inspection results.
5) Reject equipment if residues detected.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No visible residue under enhanced lighting; inspection documented with date and inspector ID.
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_206

Title: Cleaning Validation – Documentation of Cleaning Failures and Recleaning
1. Purpose: To define handling and documentation of cleaning failures.
2. Scope: All cleaning validation and routine cleaning activities.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify cleaning failure based on visual inspection or analytical results exceeding limits.
2) Document failure in deviation system.
3) Perform recleaning using validated procedure.
4) Resample and analyze surfaces.
5) Close deviation after successful recleaning and investigation.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Recleaning results within limits; root cause identified; CAPA implemented within 30 days.
5. References: QC_SOP_010

Title: Cleaning Validation – Evaluation of Cleaning Agent Residual Odor
1. Purpose: To assess potential residual odor from cleaning agents that may affect product quality.
2. Scope: Equipment used for products sensitive to odor contamination.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform cleaning using standard procedure.
2) Allow equipment to dry completely.
3) Conduct sensory evaluation by trained personnel.
4) Correlate findings with analytical data if needed.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No detectable odor; analytical confirmation of detergent residue below limit.
5. References: PIC/S PI 006

Title: Cleaning Validation – Periodic Review of Cleaning Validation Status
1. Purpose: To ensure continued validity of cleaning validation over time.
2. Scope: All validated cleaning processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Review validation data and routine verification results annually.
2) Assess changes in products, equipment, or procedures.
3) Identify need for revalidation.
4) Document review and conclusions.
5) Obtain QA approval.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Annual review completed within 12 months; revalidation triggered where applicable.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Cleaning Validation – Evaluation of Water Quality for Cleaning
1. Purpose: To ensure water used in cleaning processes meets required quality standards.
2. Scope: All water sources used for cleaning (PW, WFI).
3. Procedure:
1) Sample water from use points.
2) Perform chemical and microbial analysis.
3) Compare results with specifications.
4) Document findings.
5) Investigate deviations.
4. Acceptance Criteria: PW ≤ 100 CFU/mL; TOC ≤ 500 ppb; conductivity within limits.
5. References: USP <1231>

Title: Cleaning Validation – Cleaning Agent Compatibility with Product Residues
1. Purpose: To verify that cleaning agents effectively remove specific product residues.
2. Scope: All products manufactured on shared equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform solubility testing of product in cleaning agent.
2) Conduct bench-scale cleaning experiments.
3) Evaluate residue removal efficiency.
4) Document compatibility results.
5) Select optimal cleaning agent.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residue removal ≥ 99.0 %; no adverse reaction between agent and residue.
5. References: FDA Guidance

Title: Cleaning Validation – Control of Cleaning Materials and Tools
1. Purpose: To ensure cleaning tools do not introduce contamination.
2. Scope: Brushes, cloths, and other cleaning tools.
3. Procedure:
1) Use dedicated or disposable tools where applicable.
2) Clean and sanitize reusable tools.
3) Store tools in controlled environment.
4) Inspect tools before use.
5) Document usage.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Tools free of visible contamination; microbial count ≤ 10 CFU per tool.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Cleaning Validation – Evaluation of Residue Solubility Limits
1. Purpose: To determine solubility limits of residues for effective cleaning.
2. Scope: All products requiring cleaning validation.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform solubility testing in various solvents.
2) Identify optimal solvent for cleaning.
3) Document solubility profile.
4) Use findings in cleaning procedure design.
5) Validate effectiveness.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Solubility ≥ required threshold for removal; documented justification.
5. References: PIC/S PI 006

Title: Cleaning Validation – Verification of Cleaning Water Temperature
1. Purpose: To ensure cleaning water temperature is within validated range.
2. Scope: All cleaning processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Measure water temperature during cleaning.
2) Record values.
3) Compare with validated range.
4) Adjust process if needed.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Temperature within ±5 °C of validated value.
5. References: QC_SOP_214

Title: Cleaning Validation – Equipment Disassembly Requirements for Cleaning
1. Purpose: To define requirements for equipment disassembly prior to cleaning.
2. Scope: Equipment with complex assemblies.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify parts requiring disassembly.
2) Perform disassembly per SOP.
3) Clean individual components.
4) Reassemble equipment.
5) Verify cleanliness.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All parts accessible for cleaning; no residue detected.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Cleaning Validation – Validation Protocol Preparation
1. Purpose: To standardize preparation of cleaning validation protocols.
2. Scope: All cleaning validation studies.
3. Procedure:
1) Define scope, equipment, and products.
2) Specify sampling methods and locations.
3) Establish acceptance criteria.
4) Obtain QA approval.
5) Execute protocol.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Protocol approved prior to execution; all parameters defined.
5. References: QC_SOP_210

Title: Cleaning Validation – Final Report Review and Approval
1. Purpose: To ensure completeness and accuracy of cleaning validation reports.
2. Scope: All completed cleaning validation studies.
3. Procedure:
1) Compile all data and results.
2) Review calculations and conclusions.
3) Verify compliance with protocol.
4) Obtain QA approval.
5) Archive report.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No critical errors; report approved within 30 days.
5. References: QC_SOP_210

Title: Cleaning Validation – Periodic Cleaning Verification Program
1. Purpose: To define a risk-based program for routine verification of cleaning effectiveness after initial validation.
2. Scope: All equipment with completed cleaning validation used in routine manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Establish verification frequency based on risk (e.g., product potency, campaign length, equipment complexity).
2) Select representative worst-case locations per QC_SOP_221 for swab/rinse sampling.
3) Perform sampling post-cleaning on scheduled batches and analyze using validated methods.
4) Trend results against historical data and alert/action limits.
5) Initiate deviation and CAPA for any results exceeding specifications or adverse trends.
4. Acceptance Criteria: ≥ 95.0 % of results within limits; no two consecutive results exceeding alert limits; investigations completed within 30 days.
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_215

Title: Cleaning Validation – Verification of Rinse Conductivity and TOC
1. Purpose: To ensure final rinse water quality indicates adequate removal of residues and detergents.
2. Scope: Equipment cleaned using aqueous systems with final rinse.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect final rinse samples using defined volume and locations.
2) Measure conductivity and TOC using calibrated instruments.
3) Compare results with baseline water values and validated limits.
4) Document results in batch record.
5) Investigate excursions and repeat rinse if required.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Conductivity within ±10 % of purified water baseline; TOC ≤ 500 ppb or method-specific limit; no increasing trend over three batches.
5. References: USP <643>, USP <645>

Title: Cleaning Validation – Verification of Cleaning Agent Concentration
1. Purpose: To confirm cleaning solutions are prepared at validated concentrations.
2. Scope: All cleaning processes utilizing chemical detergents.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare cleaning solution using calibrated volumetric equipment.
2) Measure concentration using validated titration or spectroscopic method.
3) Record concentration prior to use and at defined intervals during cleaning.
4) Compare results to validated range.
5) Adjust or remake solution if out of range.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Concentration within ±10.0 % of validated target; measurements documented for each batch.
5. References: QC_SOP_214

Title: Cleaning Validation – Control of Cleaning Water Quality Excursions
1. Purpose: To manage and assess impact of water quality excursions during cleaning.
2. Scope: All cleaning operations using PW or WFI.
3. Procedure:
1) Detect excursion via online monitoring or periodic testing (TOC, conductivity, bioburden).
2) Quarantine affected cleaning events and identify impacted equipment.
3) Assess risk to cleaning effectiveness and potential residue carryover.
4) Perform additional verification sampling if required.
5) Document investigation and implement CAPA.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Excursion assessed within 24 hours; additional samples meet residue limits; CAPA effectiveness verified.
5. References: USP <1231>, QC_SOP_238

Title: Cleaning Validation – Lifecycle Management and Continued Process Verification
1. Purpose: To ensure ongoing control of cleaning processes through lifecycle management.
2. Scope: All validated cleaning processes across facility.
3. Procedure:
1) Maintain state of control through routine verification per QC_SOP_246.
2) Review trends, deviations, and changes quarterly.
3) Update risk assessments and sampling plans based on data.
4) Implement improvements via change control where needed.
5) Document lifecycle reviews and obtain QA approval.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Quarterly review completed; no unresolved adverse trends; changes approved before implementation.
5. References: ICH Q10, EU Annex 15

Title: Equipment Qualification – User Requirement Specification (URS) Development
1. Purpose: To define user requirements for equipment to ensure it meets intended GMP use.
2. Scope: All new equipment to be qualified for manufacturing or QC.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify process needs, capacity, materials of construction, and regulatory requirements.
2) Define functional, operational, and data integrity requirements.
3) Include calibration, maintenance, and safety needs.
4) Review URS with stakeholders (QC, QA, Engineering).
5) Approve URS prior to procurement.
4. Acceptance Criteria: URS complete, unambiguous, and approved by QA; traceable to design and qualification documents.
5. References: EU Annex 15, GAMP 5

Title: Equipment Qualification – Design Qualification (DQ)
1. Purpose: To verify that proposed equipment design meets URS and regulatory requirements.
2. Scope: All equipment prior to installation.
3. Procedure:
1) Review vendor design specifications against URS.
2) Evaluate materials, utilities, and control systems.
3) Assess risks and mitigation measures.
4) Document compliance matrix linking URS to design.
5) Approve DQ prior to purchase/installation.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % URS traceability; identified risks mitigated; DQ report approved by QA.
5. References: EU Annex 15, GAMP 5

Title: Equipment Qualification – Installation Qualification (IQ)
1. Purpose: To verify equipment is installed according to design specifications and manufacturer recommendations.
2. Scope: All new or relocated equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify equipment location, utilities, and connections (power, gases, water).
2) Check components against packing list and drawings.
3) Record equipment identification and calibration status of instruments.
4) Review manuals, certificates, and documentation.
5) Compile IQ report with deviations and resolutions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All components installed per specification; utilities within required ranges; documentation complete.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Equipment Qualification – Operational Qualification (OQ)
1. Purpose: To demonstrate equipment operates as intended across defined operating ranges.
2. Scope: All critical process and analytical equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Define critical operating parameters and acceptance ranges.
2) Execute test scripts covering minimum, nominal, and maximum conditions.
3) Challenge alarms, interlocks, and control functions.
4) Record results and deviations.
5) Summarize OQ outcomes in report.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All functions operate within specified limits; alarms trigger at setpoints; no unresolved critical deviations.
5. References: EU Annex 15, GAMP 5

Title: Equipment Qualification – Performance Qualification (PQ)
1. Purpose: To confirm equipment performs consistently under routine production conditions.
2. Scope: Equipment used in manufacturing or QC testing.
3. Procedure:
1) Run at least three consecutive batches or test runs under normal conditions.
2) Monitor critical quality attributes and process parameters.
3) Collect and analyze data for consistency.
4) Compare results against predefined acceptance criteria.
5) Document PQ report and obtain QA approval.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 3/3 runs meet all criteria; variability within established limits; no critical deviations.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Equipment Qualification – Calibration Management
1. Purpose: To ensure measuring instruments maintain accuracy through calibration.
2. Scope: All critical instruments associated with qualified equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Establish calibration schedule based on risk and manufacturer guidance.
2) Perform calibration using traceable standards.
3) Record as-found and as-left conditions.
4) Adjust instruments if out of tolerance.
5) Maintain calibration records and labels.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Instruments within ± specified tolerance; no overdue calibrations; traceability maintained.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Equipment Qualification – Preventive Maintenance Program
1. Purpose: To maintain equipment reliability and performance.
2. Scope: All qualified equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Develop maintenance schedule per manufacturer recommendations.
2) Perform routine inspections, lubrication, and part replacements.
3) Record maintenance activities in logbook.
4) Verify performance post-maintenance.
5) Update maintenance history.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % adherence to schedule; no critical failures due to missed maintenance.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Equipment Qualification – Change Control for Equipment Modifications
1. Purpose: To manage changes to qualified equipment and assess impact on validated state.
2. Scope: All modifications to equipment, software, or utilities.
3. Procedure:
1) Initiate change request with detailed description.
2) Perform impact and risk assessment.
3) Define requalification requirements (partial/full).
4) Execute required testing and update documentation.
5) Obtain QA approval before release.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Changes approved prior to implementation; requalification meets acceptance criteria; documentation updated.
5. References: ICH Q10, QC_SOP_099

Title: Equipment Qualification – Data Integrity for Equipment Systems
1. Purpose: To ensure electronic data generated by equipment is reliable and compliant.
2. Scope: All computerized systems associated with equipment (e.g., CDS, PLC).
3. Procedure:
1) Verify user access controls and unique IDs.
2) Enable and review audit trails for critical actions.
3) Validate data backup and recovery procedures.
4) Test electronic signatures where applicable.
5) Document system validation and controls.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Compliance with ALCOA principles; audit trails enabled; successful backup/recovery tests.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 11, GAMP 5

Title: Equipment Qualification – Deviation Handling During Qualification
1. Purpose: To manage and document deviations encountered during IQ/OQ/PQ activities.
2. Scope: All qualification protocols and reports.
3. Procedure:
1) Record deviation details, including test step and observed result.
2) Assess impact on equipment performance and qualification outcome.
3) Define corrective actions and re-testing if required.
4) Document resolution and justification for acceptance/rejection.
5) Obtain QA approval for closure.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All deviations resolved or justified; no unresolved critical deviations; impact assessed and documented.
5. References: QC_SOP_010

Title: Equipment Qualification – Utility Qualification (Clean Steam, PW, WFI)
1. Purpose: To qualify critical utilities supplying equipment to ensure consistent quality and compliance with pharmacopeial standards.
2. Scope: Clean steam, purified water (PW), and water for injection (WFI) systems connected to manufacturing and QC equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Define URS for each utility including flow, pressure, temperature, and quality attributes.
2) Perform IQ to verify installation, piping slopes, materials (e.g., SS316L), and instruments.
3) Execute OQ including alarm checks, flow/pressure ranges, and sanitization cycles.
4) Conduct PQ with routine sampling at use points for chemical (TOC, conductivity) and microbiological quality.
5) Trend data and document qualification report.
4. Acceptance Criteria: WFI endotoxin ≤ 0.25 EU/mL; PW bioburden ≤ 100 CFU/mL; parameters within ±10 % of setpoints; no adverse trends.
5. References: USP <1231>, EU Annex 15

Title: Equipment Qualification – Temperature Mapping of Ovens and Refrigerators
1. Purpose: To demonstrate uniform temperature distribution in controlled storage equipment.
2. Scope: Ovens, incubators, refrigerators, and freezers used in QC and manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Place calibrated probes at representative locations (corners, center, worst-case).
2) Run empty and loaded mapping for ≥ 24 hours.
3) Record continuous temperature data and analyze min/max and uniformity.
4) Identify hot/cold spots and adjust settings if required.
5) Document mapping report and set operating ranges.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Uniformity within ±2.0 °C (or ±5.0 °C for freezers); no excursions beyond alarm limits during study.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_184

Title: Equipment Qualification – Compressed Air System Qualification
1. Purpose: To ensure compressed air used in product-contact applications meets particulate, oil, and microbial limits.
2. Scope: All compressed air systems supplying manufacturing equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Define quality classes per ISO 8573 (particles, oil, water).
2) Perform IQ to verify filtration, dryers, and distribution piping.
3) Execute OQ including pressure/flow challenges and alarm checks.
4) Conduct PQ sampling for particulates, oil content, and microbiological quality at use points.
5) Trend results and approve system for use.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Particle count per ISO class; oil ≤ 0.01 mg/m³; microbial ≤ 1 CFU/1000 L at critical points.
5. References: ISO 8573, EU Annex 1

Title: Equipment Qualification – Alarm and Interlock Challenge Testing
1. Purpose: To verify functionality of safety alarms and interlocks on equipment.
2. Scope: All critical process and laboratory equipment with alarms/interlocks.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify all alarms and interlocks from design documents.
2) Simulate out-of-range conditions to trigger each alarm.
3) Verify visual/audible alarms and system responses (shutdown/hold).
4) Record setpoints, trigger points, and reset functionality.
5) Document results and deviations.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % alarms/interlocks trigger at defined setpoints (±5 % tolerance); system response as designed.
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_254

Title: Equipment Qualification – Software Configuration Management
1. Purpose: To control configuration of equipment software ensuring validated state is maintained.
2. Scope: PLCs, SCADA, CDS, and embedded software in equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Define baseline configuration and version control.
2) Restrict access via role-based permissions.
3) Record configuration changes via change control.
4) Perform regression testing after changes.
5) Maintain configuration log and backups.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No unauthorized changes; successful regression testing; complete audit trail available.
5. References: GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Equipment Qualification – Spare Parts Management for Critical Components
1. Purpose: To ensure availability and traceability of critical spare parts affecting equipment performance.
2. Scope: Critical components (sensors, pumps, valves) for qualified equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify critical spare parts and define minimum stock levels.
2) Qualify suppliers and verify part specifications.
3) Store parts under controlled conditions.
4) Record part usage and linkage to equipment ID.
5) Requalify equipment function after replacement if required.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No stockouts for critical parts; parts meet specifications; post-replacement checks within acceptance limits.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_258

Title: Equipment Qualification – Cleaning Verification Post-Maintenance
1. Purpose: To confirm equipment cleanliness after maintenance activities before returning to service.
2. Scope: All equipment opened or serviced during maintenance.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform cleaning per validated procedure following maintenance.
2) Conduct visual inspection under ≥ 1000 lux lighting.
3) Collect swab samples at exposed/internal surfaces.
4) Analyze for residues and, where applicable, microbial contamination.
5) Document results and release equipment.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No visible residue; chemical residues below limits; microbial counts ≤ 10 CFU/25 cm² (or stricter per area).
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_206

Title: Equipment Qualification – Verification of Utility Failover Systems
1. Purpose: To ensure backup utilities (e.g., power, chilled water) maintain equipment operation during failures.
2. Scope: Equipment connected to redundant or backup utilities.
3. Procedure:
1) Simulate primary utility failure (e.g., power cutover to UPS/generator).
2) Verify seamless transfer and equipment operation continuity.
3) Monitor critical parameters during transition.
4) Record downtime, if any, and system recovery.
5) Document test results and corrective actions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No loss of critical function; transfer time within validated limits (e.g., ≤ 10 seconds); parameters remain within ranges.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Weighing Balances
1. Purpose: To ensure balances used for GMP weighing are accurate and suitable.
2. Scope: Analytical and top-loading balances in QC and production.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform IQ for installation and leveling.
2) Execute OQ with calibration weights across range.
3) Conduct PQ using routine weighing scenarios.
4) Implement daily verification checks with standard weights.
5) Maintain calibration records and logs.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Accuracy within ±0.1 % (analytical) or per spec; repeatability %RSD ≤ 0.2 %; daily checks within tolerance.
5. References: USP <41>, QC_SOP_256

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of pH Meters
1. Purpose: To verify accuracy and reliability of pH meters used in QC testing.
2. Scope: All pH meters in laboratory environments.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform installation checks and electrode inspection.
2) Calibrate using at least two buffers bracketing sample pH.
3) Verify slope and offset values.
4) Conduct precision checks with replicate measurements.
5) Document results and maintain logs.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Slope 95–105 %; offset within ±30 mV; replicate %RSD ≤ 1.0 %.
5. References: USP <791>, QC_SOP_256

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of HPLC Systems
1. Purpose: To ensure HPLC systems perform reliably for analytical testing.
2. Scope: All HPLC/UHPLC systems in QC.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform IQ to verify modules (pump, autosampler, detector) installation.
2) Execute OQ including flow accuracy, gradient proportioning, wavelength accuracy.
3) Conduct system suitability tests (e.g., resolution, tailing).
4) Perform PQ with routine methods and samples.
5) Document qualification reports.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Flow accuracy ±2.0 %; wavelength accuracy ±2 nm; system suitability per method (e.g., resolution ≥ 2.0, %RSD ≤ 2.0 %).
5. References: USP <621>, QC_SOP_079

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Autoclaves (Sterilizers)
1. Purpose: To validate sterilization performance of autoclaves used for media and equipment.
2. Scope: All steam sterilizers in QC and manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform IQ for installation and utilities.
2) Execute OQ including temperature/pressure mapping and control tests.
3) Conduct PQ using biological indicators (e.g., Geobacillus stearothermophilus).
4) Verify load configurations and cycle parameters.
5) Document results and approve cycles.
4. Acceptance Criteria: F0 ≥ 12 minutes (or validated value); complete BI kill; temperature uniformity within ±1.0 °C during exposure.
5. References: EU Annex 1, ISO 17665

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Incubators for Microbiology
1. Purpose: To ensure incubators maintain required conditions for microbial growth.
2. Scope: All incubators used for EM and microbiological testing.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform temperature mapping at 20–25 °C and 30–35 °C setpoints.
2) Verify alarm setpoints and recovery times.
3) Test door-opening impact and stabilization.
4) Conduct PQ with growth promotion tests.
5) Document qualification.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Temperature uniformity ±2.0 °C; recovery ≤ 15 minutes; growth promotion meets USP criteria.
5. References: USP <71>, QC_SOP_184

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Refrigerated Centrifuges
1. Purpose: To verify performance of centrifuges including temperature control and RPM accuracy.
2. Scope: All centrifuges used in sample preparation.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify installation and rotor compatibility.
2) Measure RPM accuracy using tachometer.
3) Validate temperature control across range.
4) Perform load tests with representative samples.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: RPM accuracy ±5 %; temperature ±2.0 °C; no excessive vibration or imbalance.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of TOC Analyzers
1. Purpose: To ensure TOC analyzers provide accurate measurement for water quality and cleaning validation.
2. Scope: All TOC analyzers in QC.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform installation checks and reagent verification.
2) Calibrate using certified standards across range.
3) Verify system suitability and precision.
4) Conduct recovery tests with spiked samples.
5) Document qualification.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Accuracy within ±5 %; precision %RSD ≤ 5.0 %; recovery 90–110 %.
5. References: USP <643>

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Spectrophotometers (UV-Vis)
1. Purpose: To ensure UV-Vis spectrophotometers provide accurate and reliable absorbance and wavelength measurements for QC analysis.
2. Scope: All UV-Vis spectrophotometers used in analytical testing.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform IQ to verify installation, power supply, and documentation.
2) Execute OQ including wavelength accuracy using holmium oxide filter and photometric accuracy using certified standards.
3) Assess baseline noise and stray light using appropriate reference materials.
4) Conduct PQ with routine sample analyses and replicate measurements.
5) Document qualification results and maintain calibration records.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Wavelength accuracy ±1 nm; photometric accuracy ±0.005 AU; %RSD ≤ 1.0 % for replicate readings.
5. References: USP <857>, QC_SOP_256

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Dissolution Apparatus
1. Purpose: To verify performance of dissolution testing equipment used for solid dosage forms.
2. Scope: All USP Apparatus 1 and 2 dissolution systems.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform mechanical calibration including shaft alignment, basket/paddle dimensions, and rotation speed.
2) Conduct temperature mapping of dissolution medium.
3) Execute performance verification test (PVT) using USP reference tablets.
4) Record dissolution profiles and compare with acceptance ranges.
5) Document qualification and approve for routine use.
4. Acceptance Criteria: RPM accuracy ±4 %; temperature 37.0 ± 0.5 °C; PVT results within USP acceptance ranges.
5. References: USP <711>, USP <1058>

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Karl Fischer Titrators
1. Purpose: To ensure accurate determination of water content using Karl Fischer titration.
2. Scope: All volumetric and coulometric KF titrators.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify installation and reagent compatibility.
2) Calibrate using certified water standards.
3) Perform system suitability tests including drift determination.
4) Analyze replicate samples for precision assessment.
5) Document results and approve system.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Accuracy within ±3.0 % of standard; drift ≤ 10 µg/min; %RSD ≤ 3.0 %.
5. References: USP <921>, QC_SOP_256

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Gas Chromatography Systems
1. Purpose: To verify performance of GC systems for volatile compound analysis.
2. Scope: All GC instruments in QC laboratories.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform IQ to confirm installation and gas connections.
2) Execute OQ including oven temperature accuracy, flow rate, and detector response.
3) Conduct system suitability tests with standard mixtures.
4) Perform PQ using routine samples.
5) Document results and approve system.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Temperature accuracy ±2 °C; flow rate ±5 %; resolution ≥ 1.5; %RSD ≤ 2.0 %.
5. References: USP <621>, QC_SOP_079

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Particle Counters
1. Purpose: To ensure accuracy of non-viable particle monitoring instruments.
2. Scope: All particle counters used in cleanroom monitoring.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify installation and calibration status.
2) Perform flow rate verification.
3) Test counting efficiency using calibration aerosols.
4) Conduct zero count test with HEPA-filtered air.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Flow rate ±5 %; counting efficiency ≥ 50 % at 0.5 µm; zero count ≤ 1 particle.
5. References: ISO 14644-3

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Autoclave Load Configurations
1. Purpose: To validate sterilization effectiveness for different load types.
2. Scope: All load configurations used in autoclaves.
3. Procedure:
1) Define worst-case load patterns.
2) Place biological indicators and temperature probes within load.
3) Run sterilization cycle.
4) Analyze BI results and temperature data.
5) Document qualification.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Complete BI kill; temperature uniformity ±1.0 °C; F0 achieved.
5. References: ISO 17665, EU Annex 1

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Laminar Airflow Cabinets
1. Purpose: To verify performance of laminar airflow hoods used for aseptic operations.
2. Scope: All ISO 5 laminar airflow cabinets.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform airflow velocity measurements across working area.
2) Conduct HEPA filter integrity testing.
3) Execute smoke studies to confirm unidirectional flow.
4) Perform viable and non-viable monitoring.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Air velocity 0.36–0.54 m/s; HEPA integrity ≤ 0.01 % leakage; ISO 5 particle limits met.
5. References: EU Annex 1, ISO 14644

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Refrigerators for Sample Storage
1. Purpose: To ensure stable storage conditions for temperature-sensitive samples.
2. Scope: All refrigerators used for QC sample storage.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform temperature mapping with calibrated probes.
2) Monitor temperature continuously for ≥ 24 hours.
3) Verify alarm functionality.
4) Assess recovery after door opening.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Temperature 2–8 °C; uniformity ±2 °C; alarm triggered at defined limits.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Freezers (-20 °C / -80 °C)
1. Purpose: To verify performance of freezers used for sample and reagent storage.
2. Scope: All laboratory freezers.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform temperature mapping across storage space.
2) Verify setpoint accuracy and stability.
3) Test alarm and backup systems.
4) Assess recovery after simulated door opening.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Temperature within ±5 °C of setpoint; no prolonged excursions; alarms functional.
5. References: QC_SOP_262

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Mixing Equipment
1. Purpose: To ensure mixing equipment achieves uniform blending of materials.
2. Scope: All mixers used in manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify installation and mechanical integrity.
2) Define mixing parameters (speed, time).
3) Conduct mixing trials with tracer or dye.
4) Sample at multiple locations.
5) Analyze uniformity.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Content uniformity %RSD ≤ 5.0 %; no segregation observed.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Pumps and Flow Systems
1. Purpose: To ensure accurate flow delivery in process equipment.
2. Scope: All pumps used in manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify installation and connections.
2) Measure flow rate at various settings.
3) Compare with setpoints.
4) Assess repeatability.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Flow rate accuracy ±5 %; repeatability %RSD ≤ 3.0 %.
5. References: QC_SOP_254

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Pressure Gauges and Sensors
1. Purpose: To ensure accurate pressure measurement.
2. Scope: All pressure sensors in equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate using traceable standards.
2) Verify readings at multiple points.
3) Compare with reference values.
4) Document results.
5) Label calibration status.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Accuracy within ±2.0 % of full scale; calibration traceable.
5. References: QC_SOP_256

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Temperature Sensors (RTD/Thermocouples)
1. Purpose: To ensure accurate temperature measurement.
2. Scope: All temperature sensors.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate against certified reference thermometer.
2) Verify readings across operating range.
3) Record deviations.
4) Adjust or replace if necessary.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Accuracy ±1.0 °C; calibration traceable.
5. References: QC_SOP_256

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Analytical Balances (Routine Checks)
1. Purpose: To ensure continued accuracy of balances through routine checks.
2. Scope: All balances.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform daily check with standard weights.
2) Record results.
3) Compare with tolerance.
4) Investigate deviations.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within ±0.1 %; no drift over time.
5. References: USP <41>

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification Report Compilation and Approval
1. Purpose: To standardize reporting of qualification activities.
2. Scope: All IQ/OQ/PQ studies.
3. Procedure:
1) Compile data and results.
2) Review against acceptance criteria.
3) Document deviations and resolutions.
4) Prepare final report.
5) Obtain QA approval.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Complete documentation; no unresolved critical issues.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Centrifugal Pumps for CIP Systems
1. Purpose: To verify that centrifugal pumps used in cleaning-in-place (CIP) systems deliver required flow and pressure for effective cleaning.
2. Scope: All centrifugal pumps integrated into CIP loops.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform IQ to confirm installation, alignment, and material compatibility (e.g., SS316L).
2) Measure flow rate and discharge pressure across operating range using calibrated meters.
3) Execute OQ by challenging minimum/nominal/maximum setpoints and recording stability.
4) Conduct PQ during actual CIP cycles, verifying coverage and turbulence at spray devices.
5) Document performance data and compare against validated cleaning parameters.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Flow and pressure within ±5 % of setpoints; stable operation without cavitation; CIP coverage confirmed visually or via riboflavin test.
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_231

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Spray Devices (Rotary Spray Balls)
1. Purpose: To ensure spray devices provide adequate surface coverage for effective cleaning.
2. Scope: Fixed and rotary spray devices in tanks and vessels.
3. Procedure:
1) Install spray devices per design and verify orientation.
2) Perform riboflavin coverage test under defined flow and pressure.
3) Inspect internal surfaces under UV light for unwashed areas.
4) Adjust parameters (flow/pressure/rotation) as needed.
5) Document coverage maps and finalize operating conditions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % wetted surface coverage; no shadow areas; parameters within validated ranges.
5. References: ISPE Baseline Guide, QC_SOP_214

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Mixing Tank Baffles and Agitators
1. Purpose: To confirm baffle and agitator configuration achieves required mixing performance.
2. Scope: All mixing vessels used in manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify installation and dimensions of baffles and impellers against drawings.
2) Conduct mixing studies using tracer dye or conductivity probes.
3) Measure mixing time to homogeneity at various speeds.
4) Evaluate vortex formation and air entrainment.
5) Document optimal operating parameters.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Homogeneity achieved within defined time; content uniformity %RSD ≤ 5.0 %; no excessive vortexing.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Load Cells and Weighing Modules
1. Purpose: To ensure accuracy and linearity of load cells used in process weighing.
2. Scope: Load cells integrated in tanks, hoppers, and dispensing systems.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate using certified weights across operating range.
2) Check linearity at multiple points (e.g., 20 %, 50 %, 100 %).
3) Evaluate repeatability with replicate measurements.
4) Verify zero stability and drift over time.
5) Document calibration and qualification results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Accuracy within ±0.5 % of reading; linearity R² ≥ 0.999; repeatability %RSD ≤ 0.5 %.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_256

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Temperature-Controlled Reactors
1. Purpose: To verify reactors maintain and control temperature profiles during processing.
2. Scope: Jacketed vessels and reactors with temperature control systems.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify installation of temperature sensors and control loops.
2) Perform OQ by ramping temperatures across operating range.
3) Assess control accuracy and overshoot during setpoint changes.
4) Conduct PQ with representative process conditions.
5) Document temperature profiles and control performance.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Control accuracy ±1.0 °C; overshoot ≤ 2.0 °C; stable hold within ±1.0 °C during process.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Vacuum Systems
1. Purpose: To ensure vacuum systems achieve and maintain required pressure levels.
2. Scope: Vacuum pumps and systems used in drying and filtration.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify installation and leak tightness of system.
2) Measure vacuum level at multiple points.
3) Perform leak test using pressure decay.
4) Evaluate recovery time to target vacuum.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Vacuum level within ±10 % of setpoint; leak rate ≤ validated threshold; recovery time within specification.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Filter Integrity Testers
1. Purpose: To verify accuracy of instruments used for filter integrity testing (e.g., bubble point, diffusion).
2. Scope: All integrity testers used in sterile filtration.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate pressure sensors using traceable standards.
2) Verify measurement accuracy with calibrated filters.
3) Perform repeatability tests.
4) Document instrument performance.
5) Approve for use.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Pressure accuracy ±2 %; repeatability %RSD ≤ 3.0 %; results consistent with manufacturer specifications.
5. References: EU Annex 1, QC_SOP_030

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of Clean Steam Generators
1. Purpose: To ensure clean steam generators produce steam meeting microbiological and chemical requirements.
2. Scope: All clean steam systems used for sterilization.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify installation and materials of construction.
2) Test steam quality (dryness fraction, non-condensable gases).
3) Perform microbial and endotoxin testing of condensate.
4) Monitor operating parameters.
5) Document qualification.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Endotoxin ≤ 0.25 EU/mL; dryness fraction ≥ 0.95; non-condensable gases ≤ 3.5 %.
5. References: EN 285, EU Annex 1

Title: Equipment Qualification – Qualification of HVAC System Pressure Differentials
1. Purpose: To verify pressure cascades between cleanroom areas to prevent contamination.
2. Scope: All HVAC systems in classified areas.
3. Procedure:
1) Measure pressure differentials between adjacent rooms.
2) Verify direction of airflow (higher to lower classification).
3) Record readings under at-rest and dynamic conditions.
4) Adjust dampers if needed.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Pressure differential ≥ 10–15 Pa between zones; airflow direction maintained.
5. References: EU Annex 1

Title: Equipment Qualification – Equipment Decommissioning and Dequalification
1. Purpose: To define controlled process for removing equipment from service while maintaining data integrity.
2. Scope: All equipment reaching end of lifecycle or replaced.
3. Procedure:
1) Initiate change control for decommissioning.
2) Archive all qualification, calibration, and maintenance records.
3) Remove equipment from validated systems and inventory.
4) Clean and dispose or repurpose equipment per SOP.
5) Document dequalification report.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All records archived; equipment status updated; no residual GMP impact.
5. References: ICH Q10, QC_SOP_258

Title: Raw Material Testing – Sampling of Incoming Raw Materials
1. Purpose: To define representative sampling of raw materials upon receipt.
2. Scope: All incoming raw materials and components.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify material identity and integrity upon receipt.
2) Sample using appropriate tools under controlled conditions.
3) Follow sampling plan based on lot size (e.g., ANSI/ASQ Z1.4).
4) Label samples and record details.
5) Transfer to QC for testing.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Sampling per approved plan; no contamination introduced; full traceability.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Raw Material Testing – Identity Testing by FTIR
1. Purpose: To confirm identity of raw materials using FTIR spectroscopy.
2. Scope: All materials requiring spectroscopic identification.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare sample per method.
2) Acquire FTIR spectrum.
3) Compare with reference library spectrum.
4) Evaluate match factor.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Match factor ≥ 0.95; no unexpected peaks.
5. References: USP <197>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Assay Testing by HPLC
1. Purpose: To quantify active components in raw materials.
2. Scope: APIs and critical excipients.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare sample solution.
2) Inject into HPLC system.
3) Record chromatogram.
4) Calculate assay.
5) Compare with specification.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Assay within 98.0–102.0 %.
5. References: USP <621>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Moisture Content Determination
1. Purpose: To measure moisture content in raw materials.
2. Scope: Hygroscopic materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare sample.
2) Analyze using Karl Fischer titration.
3) Record results.
4) Compare with limits.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Moisture within specified range (e.g., ≤ 2.0 %).
5. References: USP <921>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Microbial Limit Testing
1. Purpose: To assess microbial contamination of raw materials.
2. Scope: Non-sterile materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare sample.
2) Perform TAMC and TYMC testing.
3) Incubate plates.
4) Count colonies.
5) Record results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: TAMC ≤ 1000 CFU/g; TYMC ≤ 100 CFU/g.
5. References: USP <61>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Impurity Profiling by HPLC
1. Purpose: To identify and quantify related impurities in raw materials to ensure compliance with ICH Q3A/B requirements.
2. Scope: Active pharmaceutical ingredients and critical excipients with defined impurity specifications.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare sample and system suitability solutions per validated method.
2) Set HPLC conditions (column, mobile phase, gradient, wavelength) as per method.
3) Inject blank, standards, and samples; verify system suitability (resolution, tailing, %RSD).
4) Integrate peaks using validated parameters and identify impurities by relative retention time.
5) Calculate individual and total impurities and document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Resolution between critical pairs ≥ 2.0; %RSD of standard ≤ 2.0 %; each impurity and total impurities within specification limits (e.g., individual ≤ 0.5 %, total ≤ 2.0 %).
5. References: ICH Q3A, USP <621>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Residual Solvent Analysis by GC
1. Purpose: To quantify residual solvents in raw materials in accordance with ICH Q3C limits.
2. Scope: APIs and excipients potentially containing organic solvents.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare headspace or direct injection samples using validated diluent.
2) Configure GC with appropriate column and detector (e.g., FID).
3) Perform system suitability with mixed solvent standards.
4) Inject standards and samples; record chromatograms.
5) Quantify solvents using calibration curve and report results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Correlation coefficient (R²) ≥ 0.995; %RSD of standards ≤ 5.0 %; each solvent below class-specific limits per ICH Q3C.
5. References: ICH Q3C, USP <467>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Particle Size Distribution by Laser Diffraction
1. Purpose: To determine particle size distribution for materials where size impacts performance.
2. Scope: Powders and granules used in manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Disperse sample in appropriate medium or dry dispersion unit.
2) Set instrument parameters (refractive index, obscuration range).
3) Run background measurement and verify stability.
4) Analyze sample in triplicate and record D10, D50, D90 values.
5) Document results and compare with specification.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Replicate %RSD ≤ 5.0 % for D50; results within specified ranges (e.g., D50 = 50–80 µm).
5. References: ISO 13320

Title: Raw Material Testing – pH Measurement of Aqueous Materials
1. Purpose: To measure pH of aqueous raw materials to ensure consistency and compatibility.
2. Scope: Liquids and solutions requiring pH specification.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate pH meter using at least two buffers bracketing expected pH.
2) Prepare sample (dilution if required) and equilibrate to room temperature.
3) Immerse electrode, allow stabilization, and record reading.
4) Rinse electrode between samples.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: pH within specified range (e.g., 5.0–7.0); slope 95–105 %; replicate difference ≤ 0.1 pH units.
5. References: USP <791>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Loss on Drying (LOD)
1. Purpose: To determine moisture and volatile content by gravimetric analysis.
2. Scope: Raw materials where LOD is specified.
3. Procedure:
1) Weigh sample accurately in tared dish.
2) Dry in oven at specified temperature (e.g., 105 °C) for defined time.
3) Cool in desiccator and reweigh.
4) Calculate percentage loss on drying.
5) Record and compare with limits.
4. Acceptance Criteria: LOD within specification (e.g., ≤ 2.0 %); duplicate results within ±0.2 % absolute.
5. References: USP <731>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Heavy Metals Determination by ICP-MS
1. Purpose: To quantify elemental impurities to meet ICH Q3D requirements.
2. Scope: Raw materials with potential for metal contamination.
3. Procedure:
1) Digest samples using validated acid digestion method.
2) Prepare calibration standards and blanks.
3) Run ICP-MS analysis with appropriate isotopes.
4) Verify system suitability and drift.
5) Calculate concentrations and report.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Calibration R² ≥ 0.999; recovery 80.0–120.0 %; each element below permitted daily exposure limits.
5. References: ICH Q3D, USP <233>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Specific Optical Rotation
1. Purpose: To determine optical rotation for chiral substances.
2. Scope: APIs with optical activity specifications.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare solution at specified concentration and solvent.
2) Calibrate polarimeter using standard.
3) Measure rotation at defined wavelength and temperature.
4) Calculate specific rotation.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specified range (e.g., +20.0° to +25.0°); temperature controlled ±0.5 °C.
5. References: USP <781>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Melting Point Determination
1. Purpose: To verify identity and purity via melting point analysis.
