2. Scope: Solid raw materials with defined melting ranges.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare finely powdered sample.
2) Load capillary tube and place in melting point apparatus.
3) Heat at controlled rate (e.g., 1–2 °C/min near expected range).
4) Record onset and completion temperatures.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Melting range within specified limits (e.g., 120–125 °C); replicate variation ≤ 1.0 °C.
5. References: USP <741>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Bulk Density and Tapped Density
1. Purpose: To assess flow properties of powders.
2. Scope: Solid raw materials used in solid dosage forms.
3. Procedure:
1) Weigh known mass of sample and transfer to graduated cylinder.
2) Measure initial (bulk) volume.
3) Tap cylinder for defined number of taps and record tapped volume.
4) Calculate bulk and tapped densities and Carr's index.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Carr's index within specification (e.g., ≤ 20 %); replicate %RSD ≤ 5.0 %.
5. References: USP <616>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Microbial Pathogen Testing
1. Purpose: To detect specified pathogens in raw materials.
2. Scope: Materials requiring absence of pathogens (e.g., E. coli, Salmonella).
3. Procedure:
1) Enrich samples in selective media.
2) Perform selective plating and incubation.
3) Confirm presumptive colonies using biochemical/rapid methods.
4) Record presence/absence.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Absence of specified pathogens in defined sample size (e.g., 10 g).
5. References: USP <62>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Identity by Wet Chemical Tests
1. Purpose: To confirm identity using classical chemical reactions.
2. Scope: Materials with compendial identification tests.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare reagents per method.
2) Perform reaction with sample.
3) Observe color change, precipitate, or gas evolution.
4) Compare with reference standard.
5) Document observations.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Positive reaction consistent with reference; no conflicting results.
5. References: USP General Chapters

Title: Raw Material Testing – Packaging and Label Verification
1. Purpose: To ensure incoming materials are correctly labeled and packaged.
2. Scope: All received raw materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify supplier label, lot number, and COA.
2) Check packaging integrity.
3) Compare with purchase specifications.
4) Record inspection.
5) Approve or reject.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No labeling discrepancies; packaging intact; documentation complete.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Raw Material Testing – Retest Period Assignment
1. Purpose: To assign retest periods based on stability data.
2. Scope: APIs and excipients.
3. Procedure:
1) Review stability data.
2) Evaluate degradation trends.
3) Assign retest period.
4) Document justification.
5) Approve.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Retest period scientifically justified; no significant degradation observed.
5. References: ICH Q1A

Title: Raw Material Testing – Certificate of Analysis (CoA) Verification
1. Purpose: To verify supplier CoA accuracy against internal testing.
2. Scope: All incoming materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Compare supplier results with internal QC testing.
2) Evaluate discrepancies.
3) Approve or reject batch.
4) Document review.
5) Archive CoA.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Results within ±2.0 % of internal testing; no critical discrepancies.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Raw Material Testing – Sampling Tool Cleaning and Control
1. Purpose: To prevent cross-contamination during sampling.
2. Scope: All sampling tools.
3. Procedure:
1) Clean tools before use.
2) Verify cleanliness.
3) Store properly.
4) Document usage.
5) Inspect before sampling.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No visible residue; microbial count ≤ 10 CFU/tool.
5. References: QC_SOP_240

Title: Raw Material Testing – Sampling Plan Using Risk-Based Stratification
1. Purpose: To establish a statistically and risk-based sampling plan for incoming raw materials ensuring representativeness and compliance.
2. Scope: All incoming lots of APIs and excipients stored in multiple containers.
3. Procedure:
1) Classify materials by risk (e.g., criticality, supplier history, homogeneity) and assign sampling level.
2) Determine number of containers to sample using ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 or square-root-n+1 rule, as justified.
3) Use cleaned, dedicated sampling tools and perform sampling in controlled area.
4) Combine increments to form composite and retain samples; label with full traceability.
5) Document deviations, if any, and link to QC_SOP_010 for investigation.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Sampling plan approved; containers sampled per plan (±0); full traceability maintained; no evidence of cross-contamination.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_301

Title: Raw Material Testing – Near-Infrared (NIR) Rapid Identity Testing
1. Purpose: To rapidly confirm identity of raw materials using NIR spectroscopy with chemometric models.
2. Scope: Materials qualified for NIR ID under an approved model.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify instrument calibration and model validity status.
2) Scan sample through container or via sample cup per method.
3) Acquire spectrum and compare with validated library using model.
4) Review match score and residuals; flag outliers.
5) Record results and perform periodic cross-check with compendial method.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Model match score ≥ 0.95; no outlier flags; periodic verification concordance ≥ 98.0 % with compendial ID.
5. References: USP <1119>, 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Raw Material Testing – Chloride Content by Ion Chromatography
1. Purpose: To quantify chloride levels impacting product stability or process compatibility.
2. Scope: Raw materials with chloride specifications.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare sample in suitable diluent and filter if required.
2) Calibrate IC with chloride standards across range.
3) Inject blank, standards, and samples; verify system suitability.
4) Integrate peaks and calculate concentration via calibration curve.
5) Document and trend results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: R² ≥ 0.999; standard %RSD ≤ 2.0 %; results within specification (e.g., ≤ 100 ppm).
5. References: USP <621>, ICH Q2(R2)

Title: Raw Material Testing – Sulfate Determination by Turbidimetry
1. Purpose: To measure sulfate impurities using turbidimetric method.
2. Scope: Materials with sulfate limits.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare sample and reagent (e.g., barium chloride).
2) Generate turbidity under controlled conditions.
3) Measure absorbance at specified wavelength.
4) Construct calibration curve and quantify sulfate.
5) Record results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Calibration R² ≥ 0.995; duplicate difference ≤ 10 %; result within specification (e.g., ≤ 200 ppm).
5. References: USP General Chapters

Title: Raw Material Testing – Conductivity Measurement
1. Purpose: To assess ionic content of aqueous raw materials.
2. Scope: Water-based raw materials and solutions.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate conductivity meter with standard solutions.
2) Measure sample at controlled temperature (25 ± 1 °C).
3) Record stabilized reading.
4) Rinse probe between samples.
5) Document results and compare with limits.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specified range (e.g., ≤ 10 µS/cm); meter accuracy ±2 %.
5. References: USP <645>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Color Measurement by Spectrophotometry
1. Purpose: To quantify color attributes impacting product appearance.
2. Scope: Liquids and solutions with color specifications.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate instrument with blank and standards.
2) Measure sample absorbance or color index (e.g., APHA).
3) Perform triplicate readings.
4) Calculate average and %RSD.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specified color units; %RSD ≤ 2.0 %.
5. References: ASTM D1209

Title: Raw Material Testing – Viscosity Determination
1. Purpose: To determine viscosity for processability and quality control.
2. Scope: Liquid raw materials and solutions.
3. Procedure:
1) Equilibrate sample to test temperature.
2) Select appropriate viscometer and spindle.
3) Measure viscosity at defined shear rate.
4) Record readings in triplicate.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specified range (e.g., 50–150 cP); %RSD ≤ 3.0 %.
5. References: USP <911>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Density/Specific Gravity Measurement
1. Purpose: To determine density for identity and formulation calculations.
2. Scope: Liquid raw materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate densitometer or pycnometer.
2) Measure sample at controlled temperature.
3) Record readings.
4) Perform replicate measurements.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specified range; %RSD ≤ 0.5 %.
5. References: USP <841>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Identification by X-Ray Diffraction (XRD)
1. Purpose: To confirm crystalline form and identity.
2. Scope: Solid APIs with polymorphism concerns.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare finely ground sample.
2) Acquire diffraction pattern.
3) Compare with reference pattern.
4) Evaluate peak positions and intensities.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Pattern matches reference; no additional peaks indicating new polymorph.
5. References: USP <941>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Residual Moisture by Loss on Ignition (LOI)
1. Purpose: To quantify volatile and combustible residues upon ignition.
2. Scope: Inorganic materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Weigh sample in crucible.
2) Ignite at specified temperature (e.g., 550 °C).
3) Cool in desiccator and reweigh.
4) Calculate % loss.
5) Record results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specification (e.g., ≤ 1.0 %); duplicate difference ≤ 0.2 %.
5. References: USP <281>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Assay by Titration
1. Purpose: To quantify analyte using volumetric titration.
2. Scope: Materials with titrimetric assays.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare standard titrant and standardize.
2) Dissolve sample in appropriate solvent.
3) Titrate to endpoint using indicator or potentiometric detection.
4) Calculate assay.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within 98.0–102.0 %; duplicate difference ≤ 0.5 %.
5. References: USP General Chapters

Title: Raw Material Testing – Appearance and Clarity Assessment
1. Purpose: To evaluate visual quality attributes.
2. Scope: All raw materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Inspect under standardized lighting conditions.
2) Compare with reference standards.
3) Assess color, clarity, and presence of particulates.
4) Document observations.
5) Investigate deviations.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Meets description; no visible foreign matter.
5. References: EP 2.2.1

Title: Raw Material Testing – Foreign Matter Examination
1. Purpose: To detect extraneous materials.
2. Scope: Solid raw materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Spread sample on inspection surface.
2) Examine visually and with magnification.
3) Separate foreign particles.
4) Weigh or count contaminants.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: ≤ specified limit (e.g., ≤ 0.1 % w/w); no hazardous contaminants.
5. References: USP <561>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Sampling Room Environmental Control
1. Purpose: To maintain controlled environment during sampling.
2. Scope: All sampling rooms.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify room classification and cleanliness.
2) Monitor temperature and humidity.
3) Perform EM per QC_SOP_151.
4) Record conditions.
5) Investigate excursions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Conditions within specified limits; no EM excursions.
5. References: EU Annex 1

Title: Raw Material Testing – Sample Retention and Storage
1. Purpose: To ensure retained samples are properly stored for future reference.
2. Scope: All tested raw materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Label retain samples with batch details.
2) Store under specified conditions.
3) Maintain inventory log.
4) Periodically inspect condition.
5) Dispose after retention period.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Retention ≥ 1 year after expiry; no degradation observed.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Raw Material Testing – Water Content by Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA)
1. Purpose: To determine water content and volatile components using thermogravimetric analysis for materials where Karl Fischer is not suitable.
2. Scope: Solid raw materials with thermal stability profiles.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate TGA instrument with standard weights and temperature reference.
2) Weigh sample (5–20 mg) into pan and record initial mass.
3) Heat under controlled rate (e.g., 10 °C/min) up to defined temperature.
4) Record mass loss versus temperature and identify moisture loss region.
5) Calculate % water content and document thermogram.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Repeatability %RSD ≤ 3.0 %; results within specification (e.g., ≤ 2.0 % w/w); baseline drift within validated limits.
5. References: USP <731>, ICH Q2(R2)

Title: Raw Material Testing – Identification by Raman Spectroscopy
1. Purpose: To confirm identity of raw materials using Raman spectroscopy, including through-container analysis.
2. Scope: Materials qualified for Raman ID testing.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify instrument calibration using polystyrene standard.
2) Acquire spectrum from sample (direct or through container).
3) Compare spectrum to validated library using chemometric model.
4) Review match quality and spectral residuals.
5) Document results and exceptions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Match score ≥ 0.95; no outlier flags; periodic orthogonal confirmation per program.
5. References: USP <1120>, 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Raw Material Testing – Nitrogen Content by Kjeldahl Method
1. Purpose: To quantify nitrogen content for protein or amine-containing materials.
2. Scope: Raw materials requiring nitrogen specification.
3. Procedure:
1) Digest sample with sulfuric acid and catalyst.
2) Neutralize and distill liberated ammonia.
3) Titrate distillate with standardized acid.
4) Calculate % nitrogen content.
5) Record results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specification (e.g., 8.0–10.0 %); duplicate difference ≤ 0.3 % absolute.
5. References: USP <461>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Ash Content Determination
1. Purpose: To determine inorganic residue remaining after ignition.
2. Scope: Organic raw materials with ash limits.
3. Procedure:
1) Weigh sample into pre-ignited crucible.
2) Ignite at 500–600 °C until constant weight.
3) Cool in desiccator and reweigh.
4) Calculate % ash.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specified limit (e.g., ≤ 0.5 %); duplicate difference ≤ 0.1 %.
5. References: USP <281>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Identification by TLC
1. Purpose: To confirm identity using thin-layer chromatography.
2. Scope: Materials with TLC identification methods.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare sample and reference solutions.
2) Apply spots on TLC plate.
3) Develop in specified solvent system.
4) Visualize under UV or with reagents.
5) Compare Rf values and appearance.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Sample Rf matches reference within ±0.05; no extra spots above reporting threshold.
5. References: USP <201>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Determination of Sulfated Ash
1. Purpose: To quantify sulfated ash content for certain excipients.
2. Scope: Materials with sulfated ash specification.
3. Procedure:
1) Treat sample with sulfuric acid.
2) Ignite at specified temperature.
3) Cool and weigh residue.
4) Calculate % sulfated ash.
5) Record results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specification (e.g., ≤ 0.2 %); duplicate difference ≤ 0.05 %.
5. References: USP <281>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Determination of pKa by Potentiometric Titration
1. Purpose: To characterize ionization properties of raw materials.
2. Scope: APIs requiring pKa determination.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare solution at known concentration.
2) Titrate with standardized acid/base.
3) Record pH versus volume.
4) Determine pKa from titration curve.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: pKa within expected range; replicate variation ≤ 0.1 units.
5. References: ICH Q6A

Title: Raw Material Testing – Determination of Refractive Index
1. Purpose: To assess identity and purity via refractive index.
2. Scope: Liquid raw materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate refractometer.
2) Measure sample at controlled temperature.
3) Record refractive index.
4) Perform replicate readings.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specified range; %RSD ≤ 0.2 %.
5. References: USP <831>

Title: Raw Material Testing – Determination of Residual Acidity/Alkalinity
1. Purpose: To measure residual acid or base content.
2. Scope: Raw materials with pH-sensitive applications.
3. Procedure:
1) Dissolve sample in water.
2) Titrate with standardized acid/base.
3) Determine endpoint.
4) Calculate acidity/alkalinity.
5) Record results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specified limits; duplicate difference ≤ 5.0 %.
5. References: USP General Chapters

Title: Raw Material Testing – Determination of Peroxide Value
1. Purpose: To quantify peroxide content indicating oxidation.
2. Scope: Lipid-based materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Dissolve sample in solvent mixture.
2) React with iodide.
3) Titrate liberated iodine.
4) Calculate peroxide value.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: ≤ specified limit (e.g., ≤ 5 meq/kg); duplicate difference ≤ 10 %.
5. References: USP General Chapters

Title: Raw Material Testing – Determination of Saponification Value
1. Purpose: To assess fatty acid content in oils.
2. Scope: Lipid raw materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Reflux sample with alcoholic KOH.
2) Titrate excess KOH with acid.
3) Calculate saponification value.
4) Record results.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specified range; duplicate difference ≤ 5 %.
5. References: USP General Chapters

Title: Raw Material Testing – Determination of Iodine Value
1. Purpose: To measure degree of unsaturation in fats.
2. Scope: Lipid materials.
3. Procedure:
1) React sample with iodine reagent.
2) Titrate excess iodine.
3) Calculate iodine value.
4) Document results.
5) Compare with limits.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within specified range; duplicate difference ≤ 5 %.
5. References: USP General Chapters

Title: Raw Material Testing – Determination of pH Stability Over Time
1. Purpose: To evaluate pH changes during storage.
2. Scope: Aqueous materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Measure initial pH.
2) Store under defined conditions.
3) Measure pH at intervals.
4) Record changes.
5) Analyze trends.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Change ≤ ±0.5 units over defined period.
5. References: ICH Q1A

Title: Raw Material Testing – Determination of Solubility Profile
1. Purpose: To assess solubility in various solvents.
2. Scope: APIs and excipients.
3. Procedure:
1) Test solubility in water, ethanol, and other solvents.
2) Observe dissolution behavior.
3) Record qualitative and quantitative results.
4) Document findings.
5) Compare with specifications.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Meets defined solubility classification.
5. References: USP General Chapters

Title: Raw Material Testing – Final Disposition and Release Decision
1. Purpose: To define criteria for release or rejection of raw materials.
2. Scope: All tested raw materials.
3. Procedure:
1) Review all analytical results.
2) Compare with specifications.
3) Evaluate deviations.
4) Approve or reject material.
5) Document decision.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All tests within specification; QA approval obtained.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: In-Process Control – Blend Uniformity Testing
1. Purpose: To verify homogeneity of powder blends prior to compression or filling to ensure consistent dosage units.
2. Scope: All solid dosage manufacturing processes involving blending.
3. Procedure:
1) Define sampling plan covering top, middle, and bottom of blender (minimum 10 locations).
2) Collect samples using thief sampler under controlled conditions to avoid segregation.
3) Prepare samples and analyze assay by validated HPLC-UV method.
4) Calculate content uniformity and %RSD across locations.
5) Document results and investigate any atypical variability.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Individual results within 90.0–110.0 % of target; %RSD ≤ 5.0 %; no location-specific bias observed.
5. References: USP <905>, QC_SOP_303

Title: In-Process Control – Tablet Compression Weight Control
1. Purpose: To control tablet weight during compression ensuring dose accuracy.
2. Scope: All tablet compression operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Set target weight and acceptable range in batch record.
2) At defined intervals (e.g., every 15 minutes), collect 20 tablets.
3) Weigh individually using calibrated balance and calculate average and %RSD.
4) Adjust compression parameters (fill depth, force) if trend shifts.
5) Record data and actions taken.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Average within target ±5.0 %; individual units within ±10.0 %; %RSD ≤ 3.0 %.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_269

Title: In-Process Control – Tablet Hardness and Friability
1. Purpose: To ensure mechanical integrity of tablets during processing.
2. Scope: All tablet batches during compression.
3. Procedure:
1) Sample tablets at defined intervals.
2) Measure hardness using calibrated tester.
3) Conduct friability test (100 revolutions at 25 rpm).
4) Calculate % weight loss and record results.
5) Adjust process parameters if out of trend.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Hardness within 5–10 kp (or product-specific); friability ≤ 1.0 % weight loss.
5. References: USP <1217>, USP <1216>

Title: In-Process Control – Granule Moisture Content
1. Purpose: To control moisture content of granules for optimal compression.
2. Scope: Wet granulation processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect granule samples post-drying.
2) Measure moisture using loss on drying or NIR method.
3) Record results and compare with target.
4) Continue drying if above limit.
5) Document final moisture level.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Moisture within 1.5–3.0 % (product-specific); replicate difference ≤ 0.2 %.
5. References: USP <731>

Title: In-Process Control – Coating Weight Gain Monitoring
1. Purpose: To ensure consistent coating application on tablets.
2. Scope: Film and sugar coating processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Weigh tablets before coating.
2) Periodically sample tablets during coating.
3) Calculate % weight gain.
4) Adjust spray rate or pan speed if deviation observed.
5) Record data.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Weight gain within ±2.0 % of target; uniform appearance without defects.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: In-Process Control – pH Adjustment During Solution Preparation
1. Purpose: To control pH during solution preparation to ensure stability and performance.
2. Scope: Liquid manufacturing processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Measure initial pH using calibrated meter.
2) Add acid/base incrementally.
3) Mix thoroughly and re-measure.
4) Continue until target pH reached.
5) Document adjustments.
4. Acceptance Criteria: pH within target ±0.2 units; no overshoot beyond ±0.5 units.
5. References: USP <791>

Title: In-Process Control – Filtration Integrity Testing (Pre-Use)
1. Purpose: To verify integrity of filters prior to use in manufacturing.
2. Scope: Sterile and non-sterile filtration steps.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform bubble point or diffusion test.
2) Record pressure values.
3) Compare with specification.
4) Approve filter for use.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Meets manufacturer's specification; no failure permitted.
5. References: EU Annex 1, QC_SOP_030

Title: In-Process Control – Fill Volume Verification
1. Purpose: To ensure correct fill volume in liquid dosage forms.
2. Scope: Filling operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect filled units at defined intervals.
2) Measure volume or weight.
3) Calculate average and variation.
4) Adjust filling machine if needed.
5) Record results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within ±5.0 % of target; %RSD ≤ 3.0 %.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: In-Process Control – Mixing Time Determination
1. Purpose: To ensure adequate mixing time for uniformity.
2. Scope: All mixing operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Conduct time studies with sampling at intervals.
2) Analyze samples for uniformity.
3) Identify minimum mixing time.
4) Document findings.
5) Use validated time in production.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Uniformity achieved within defined time; %RSD ≤ 5.0 %.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: In-Process Control – Temperature Monitoring During Processing
1. Purpose: To ensure temperature control during manufacturing.
2. Scope: All temperature-sensitive processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Monitor temperature continuously.
2) Record data.
3) Compare with setpoints.
4) Investigate excursions.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within ±2.0 °C of target; no uninvestigated excursions.
5. References: QC_SOP_262

Title: In-Process Control – Pressure Monitoring in Filtration Systems
1. Purpose: To control pressure during filtration.
2. Scope: Filtration operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Monitor inlet and outlet pressure.
2) Record values.
3) Detect pressure drop.
4) Investigate deviations.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Within defined range; no abnormal pressure spikes.
5. References: QC_SOP_286

Title: In-Process Control – Visual Inspection of Intermediate Product
1. Purpose: To detect defects in intermediates.
2. Scope: All manufacturing stages.
3. Procedure:
1) Inspect samples visually.
2) Compare with standards.
3) Record defects.
4) Investigate issues.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No critical defects; acceptable minor defects.
5. References: EP 2.2.1

Title: In-Process Control – In-Line NIR Monitoring
1. Purpose: To monitor process parameters in real-time using NIR.
2. Scope: Continuous manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate NIR model.
2) Monitor process.
3) Record data.
4) Adjust process if needed.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Model accuracy ≥ 95 %; process within limits.
5. References: PAT Guidance

Title: In-Process Control – Sampling Frequency Determination
1. Purpose: To define sampling intervals.
2. Scope: All IPC activities.
3. Procedure:
1) Assess process variability.
2) Define sampling plan.
3) Document frequency.
4) Review periodically.
5) Update as needed.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Sampling sufficient to detect trends.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: In-Process Control – Documentation and Data Recording
1. Purpose: To ensure accurate recording of IPC data.
2. Scope: All IPC activities.
3. Procedure:
1) Record results in batch record.
2) Verify entries.
3) Review data.
4) Approve records.
5) Archive.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No missing data; entries accurate and legible.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: In-Process Control – Tablet Thickness Measurement
1. Purpose: To monitor tablet thickness to ensure uniform compression and downstream coating consistency.
2. Scope: All tablet compression batches.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect 10 tablets every 30 minutes during compression.
2) Measure thickness using calibrated digital micrometer (accuracy ±0.01 mm).
3) Record individual values and calculate mean and %RSD.
4) Compare results with target thickness range defined in batch record.
5) Adjust compression force or tooling if deviation trend observed.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Thickness within ±5.0 % of target (e.g., 4.5–5.0 mm); %RSD ≤ 2.0 %.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_352

Title: In-Process Control – Capsule Fill Weight Verification
1. Purpose: To ensure accurate fill weight of capsules during encapsulation.
2. Scope: All capsule filling operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect 20 capsules at defined intervals (e.g., every 20 minutes).
2) Weigh intact capsules, then empty and weigh shells.
3) Calculate net fill weight for each unit.
4) Determine average and %RSD.
5) Adjust dosing disk or tamping pin if results deviate.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Average within ±5.0 % of target; individual units within ±10.0 %; %RSD ≤ 4.0 %.
5. References: USP <905>

Title: In-Process Control – Granulation Endpoint Determination
1. Purpose: To determine optimal granulation endpoint during wet granulation.
2. Scope: High-shear and fluid-bed granulation processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Monitor torque or power consumption of granulator.
2) Collect granule samples at intervals.
3) Measure moisture using halogen moisture analyzer.
4) Evaluate granule size distribution using sieve analysis.
5) Stop granulation when predefined criteria met.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Moisture 18.0–22.0 % w/w (wet mass); torque plateau reached; particle size D50 within ±10 % of target.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: In-Process Control – Drying Endpoint Determination (Fluid Bed Dryer)
1. Purpose: To ensure granules reach target moisture before compression.
2. Scope: Fluid bed drying operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Set inlet temperature (e.g., 60–80 °C) and airflow.
2) Collect samples every 10 minutes.
3) Measure moisture using LOD or NIR analyzer.
4) Plot moisture vs time.
5) Stop drying at validated endpoint.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Final moisture 1.5–3.0 % w/w; drying time within validated range; no overheating (>90 °C).
5. References: USP <731>

Title: In-Process Control – Coating Defect Monitoring
1. Purpose: To detect coating defects such as picking, peeling, or color variation.
2. Scope: All tablet coating operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Sample tablets every 30 minutes during coating.
2) Inspect visually under 1000 lux lighting.
3) Record defects and frequency.
4) Correlate defects with process parameters (spray rate, pan speed).
5) Adjust parameters as needed.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Defect rate ≤ 2.0 %; uniform color and surface finish.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: In-Process Control – Dissolution Testing (At-Line)
1. Purpose: To monitor dissolution performance during manufacturing.
2. Scope: Immediate-release tablet batches.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect tablets at defined compression intervals.
2) Perform dissolution using USP Apparatus 2 (paddle) at 50 rpm in 900 mL medium.
3) Sample at specified time point (e.g., 30 minutes).
4) Analyze using UV or HPLC.
5) Record % dissolved.
4. Acceptance Criteria: ≥ 80.0 % dissolved at 30 minutes; %RSD ≤ 10.0 %.
5. References: USP <711>

Title: In-Process Control – Granule Flowability Testing
1. Purpose: To assess flow properties of granules before compression.
2. Scope: Solid dosage manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Measure angle of repose using funnel method.
2) Determine bulk and tapped density.
3) Calculate Carr's index and Hausner ratio.
4) Compare with predefined limits.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Carr's index ≤ 20 %; Hausner ratio ≤ 1.25; angle of repose ≤ 35°.
5. References: USP <616>

Title: In-Process Control – Blend Segregation Assessment
1. Purpose: To detect segregation during handling and transfer.
2. Scope: Powder blending and transfer operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Sample blend before and after transfer.
2) Analyze assay for each sample.
3) Compare variability.
4) Evaluate segregation risk.
5) Document findings.
4. Acceptance Criteria: %RSD ≤ 5.0 %; no significant shift in assay distribution.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: In-Process Control – Compression Force Monitoring
1. Purpose: To control compression force for consistent tablet properties.
2. Scope: Tablet compression machines.
3. Procedure:
1) Monitor compression force via machine sensors.
2) Record values at defined intervals.
3) Compare with target range.
4) Adjust settings if deviation occurs.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Force within ±10 % of target; no drift trend.
5. References: QC_SOP_352

Title: In-Process Control – Lubricant Distribution Check
1. Purpose: To ensure uniform distribution of lubricant in blend.
2. Scope: Final blending stage.
3. Procedure:
1) Sample blend from multiple locations.
2) Analyze lubricant content using validated method.
3) Calculate %RSD.
4) Compare with specification.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: %RSD ≤ 5.0 %; content within ±10 % of target.
5. References: ICH Q2(R2)

Title: In-Process Control – pH Monitoring During Fermentation
1. Purpose: To control pH in bioprocesses.
2. Scope: Fermentation operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Monitor pH continuously using probe.
2) Calibrate probe daily.
3) Adjust pH using acid/base addition.
4) Record values.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: pH within ±0.2 units of setpoint.
5. References: USP <791>

Title: In-Process Control – Dissolved Oxygen Monitoring
1. Purpose: To ensure adequate oxygen levels in bioprocess.
2. Scope: Fermentation systems.
3. Procedure:
1) Monitor DO using probe.
2) Calibrate sensor.
3) Adjust aeration/agitation.
4) Record data.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: DO ≥ 30 % saturation.
5. References: ICH Q7

Title: In-Process Control – Filtration Flow Rate Monitoring
1. Purpose: To ensure consistent filtration performance.
2. Scope: Filtration processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Measure flow rate.
2) Record values.
3) Compare with target.
4) Investigate deviations.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Flow within ±10 % of target.
5. References: QC_SOP_286

Title: In-Process Control – Batch Yield Calculation
1. Purpose: To calculate process yield.
2. Scope: All manufacturing batches.
3. Procedure:
1) Record input materials.
2) Measure output quantity.
3) Calculate yield.
4) Compare with expected.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Yield within ±5.0 % of theoretical.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: In-Process Control – Deviation Handling During IPC
1. Purpose: To manage IPC deviations.
2. Scope: All IPC activities.
3. Procedure:
1) Record deviation.
2) Investigate cause.
3) Implement CAPA.
4) Document.
5) Close.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Investigation within 30 days.
5. References: QC_SOP_010

Title: In-Process Control – Granule Particle Size Distribution (Sieve Analysis)
1. Purpose: To monitor particle size distribution (PSD) of granules prior to compression to ensure consistent flow and compaction.
2. Scope: All granulation processes for solid dosage forms.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect representative granule sample (≥ 100 g) from dryer discharge.
2) Assemble sieve stack (e.g., 850, 600, 425, 250 µm) and verify cleanliness.
3) Weigh sample, load onto top sieve, and run sieve shaker for 10 minutes at standardized amplitude.
4) Weigh material retained on each sieve and calculate % distribution.
5) Record D10/D50/D90 where applicable and compare to target profile.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Target fraction (e.g., 250–600 µm) ≥ 80.0 %; fines (<250 µm) ≤ 10.0 %; replicate %RSD ≤ 5.0 %.
5. References: USP <786>, QC_SOP_308

Title: In-Process Control – Tablet Content Uniformity (At-Line)
1. Purpose: To verify dosage uniformity during compression using rapid at-line assay.
2. Scope: Immediate-release tablets during routine compression.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect 10 tablets every 30 minutes.
2) Prepare samples via validated rapid extraction (e.g., UV-Vis method).
3) Measure absorbance at specified wavelength and calculate content using calibration.
4) Evaluate individual values and %RSD.
5) Adjust process if drift is observed.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Individual results 85.0–115.0 % of label claim; %RSD ≤ 6.0 %; trend within control limits.
5. References: USP <905>, QC_SOP_276

Title: In-Process Control – Compression Speed and Throughput Monitoring
1. Purpose: To control press speed to maintain tablet quality and minimize defects.
2. Scope: All rotary tablet presses.
3. Procedure:
1) Record turret speed (rpm) and tablets per minute (TPM) at start and every 30 minutes.
2) Correlate speed with hardness, weight, and defect rates.
3) Adjust feeder speed and compression force if deviations occur.
4) Document settings and changes.
5) Review trends at end of batch.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Speed within validated range (e.g., 30–60 rpm); no increase in defect rate > 2.0 %.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: In-Process Control – Capsule Lock Length and Closure Integrity
1. Purpose: To ensure capsules are properly locked and sealed during filling.
2. Scope: Hard gelatin capsule filling operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect 20 capsules every 30 minutes.
2) Measure lock length using digital caliper (±0.01 mm).
3) Perform manual twist test to assess closure integrity.
4) Inspect for cap/body separation or dents.
5) Record results and adjust machine settings if needed.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Lock length within ±0.2 mm of target; 0 failures in twist test; defect rate ≤ 1.0 %.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: In-Process Control – Spray Rate and Atomization Monitoring (Coating)
1. Purpose: To control coating spray rate and atomization for uniform film formation.
2. Scope: Tablet coating processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Set spray rate (e.g., 100–300 g/min) and atomization air pressure per batch record.
2) Verify nozzle performance and droplet formation.
3) Record spray rate and pressure every 15 minutes.
4) Observe bed moisture and tablet surface condition.
5) Adjust parameters to avoid overwetting or spray drying.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Spray rate within ±10.0 %; atomization pressure within ±0.2 bar; no visible defects.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: In-Process Control – Inlet/Exhaust Air Parameters (Fluid Bed)
1. Purpose: To ensure stable drying conditions in fluid bed operations.
2. Scope: Fluid bed dryers and granulators.
3. Procedure:
1) Monitor inlet temperature (e.g., 60–80 °C), exhaust temperature, and airflow.
2) Record values every 10 minutes via SCADA.
3) Verify filters are clean and pressure drop is within limits.
4) Adjust airflow/temperature to maintain target drying curve.
5) Document any excursions and actions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Inlet temp ±3.0 °C; exhaust temp within validated profile; filter ΔP within limits.
5. References: QC_SOP_262

Title: In-Process Control – Solution Concentration Verification by Refractometry
1. Purpose: To confirm concentration of process solutions (e.g., sugar or polymer solutions) during preparation.
2. Scope: Liquid preparation steps for coating or granulation.
3. Procedure:
1) Calibrate refractometer at 20–25 °C.
2) Collect sample from mixing vessel after homogenization.
3) Measure refractive index or Brix value in triplicate.
4) Convert to concentration using calibration curve.
5) Record and compare to target.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Concentration within ±2.0 % of target; %RSD ≤ 1.0 %.
5. References: USP <831>

Title: In-Process Control – Metal Detection Sensitivity Check
1. Purpose: To verify sensitivity of metal detectors used on finished units.
2. Scope: Tablet/capsule packaging lines with metal detectors.
3. Procedure:
1) Challenge detector with certified test pieces (Fe 1.5 mm, Non-Fe 2.0 mm, SS 2.5 mm or per product).
2) Pass test pieces through center and edges of aperture.
3) Confirm rejection mechanism functions.
4) Record results at start, hourly, and end of run.
5) Stop line and investigate failures.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % detection and rejection of all test pieces; no missed detections.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: In-Process Control – Leak Test for Blister Packs
1. Purpose: To ensure integrity of blister packaging preventing moisture/oxygen ingress.
2. Scope: Blister packaging operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect blister samples every hour.
2) Perform vacuum leak test (e.g., 200–300 mbar for 30–60 seconds).
3) Observe for bubble formation or dye ingress.
4) Record pass/fail results.
5) Adjust sealing temperature/pressure if failures occur.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 0 leaks in sample set; sealing parameters within validated range.
5. References: ASTM D3078

Title: In-Process Control – Label Verification During Packaging
1. Purpose: To ensure correct labels are applied to products.
2. Scope: All packaging lines.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify label artwork, batch number, and expiry date at line start.
2) Perform in-process checks every 30 minutes.
3) Use barcode scanner where applicable to confirm correctness.
4) Segregate and investigate any mismatches.
5) Document checks in batch record.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 0 labeling errors; 100 % barcode readability; checks performed per schedule.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: In-Process Control – Sieve Integrity Check (Milling/Sieving)
1. Purpose: To ensure sieves are intact to prevent oversized particles or foreign matter.
2. Scope: Milling and sieving operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Inspect sieve mesh visually before and after use.
2) Verify mesh size against specification.
3) Perform integrity check using light inspection.
4) Document inspection results.
5) Replace damaged sieves immediately.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No tears or deformation; correct mesh size; documented checks before/after use.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: In-Process Control – Line Clearance Verification
1. Purpose: To confirm removal of previous product and materials before batch start.
2. Scope: All manufacturing and packaging lines.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform visual inspection of equipment and area.
2) Verify removal of previous labels, components, and documents.
3) Cross-check against line clearance checklist.
4) QA performs independent verification.
5) Document clearance approval prior to start.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % checklist completion; QA sign-off; no foreign materials present.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: In-Process Control – Environmental Conditions Monitoring (Temperature/Humidity)
1. Purpose: To maintain environmental conditions within limits affecting product quality.
2. Scope: Manufacturing and packaging areas.
3. Procedure:
1) Monitor temperature and RH using calibrated sensors.
2) Record data continuously or at defined intervals (≤ 30 minutes).
3) Review alarms for excursions.
4) Investigate deviations and assess impact.
5) Document and trend conditions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Temperature within ±2.0 °C; RH within ±5.0 % of setpoint; no uninvestigated excursions.
5. References: EU Annex 1

Title: In-Process Control – Powder Blend Segregation During Transfer
1. Purpose: To assess segregation risk during pneumatic or gravity transfer.
2. Scope: Transfer of blends from blender to hopper.
3. Procedure:
1) Sample blend pre- and post-transfer at ≥ 5 locations.
2) Analyze assay using validated method.
3) Compare mean and variability.
4) Evaluate segregation index.
5) Document findings and adjust transfer parameters if needed.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Mean shift ≤ ±2.0 %; %RSD ≤ 5.0 %; no systematic bias.
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_373

Title: In-Process Control – Reconciliation of Printed Components
1. Purpose: To ensure accurate accounting of printed packaging components.
2. Scope: Labels, leaflets, cartons.
3. Procedure:
1) Count issued components at line start.
2) Track used, rejected, and returned quantities during run.
3) Perform final reconciliation at line end.
4) Investigate discrepancies immediately.
5) Document reconciliation.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Discrepancy ≤ 0.1 % or justified; all variances investigated and approved.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: In-Process Control – Intermediate Hold Time Verification
1. Purpose: To ensure intermediate materials remain within validated hold times without impacting quality.
2. Scope: All intermediates held between manufacturing steps.
3. Procedure:
1) Record start time of hold after processing step completion.
2) Store material under defined environmental conditions (e.g., 20–25 °C, RH ≤ 60 %).
3) Monitor temperature and humidity at ≤ 30-minute intervals.
4) Sample material at defined timepoints for key attributes (assay, moisture).
5) Compare results with initial values and validated hold time limits.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Hold time ≤ validated maximum (e.g., 48 hours); assay change ≤ ±2.0 %; moisture change ≤ ±0.5 %.
5. References: ICH Q1A, QC_SOP_354

Title: In-Process Control – Lubrication Time Optimization
1. Purpose: To control blending time of lubricant to avoid over-lubrication affecting tablet hardness and dissolution.
2. Scope: Final blending stage in solid dosage manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Set initial lubrication time (e.g., 3–10 minutes) based on validation.
2) Collect blend samples at defined intervals (e.g., 2, 5, 8 minutes).
3) Analyze dissolution and hardness of compressed tablets.
4) Identify optimal lubrication time with minimal impact on CQAs.
5) Document final parameter in batch record.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Dissolution ≥ 80.0 % at Q-time; hardness within 5–10 kp; no trend of over-lubrication.
5. References: USP <711>, QC_SOP_353

Title: In-Process Control – Hopper Level Monitoring During Compression
1. Purpose: To ensure consistent feed of blend into tablet press.
2. Scope: Tablet compression operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Monitor hopper level using sensor or visual indicator.
2) Maintain level within defined range (e.g., 30–70 % capacity).
3) Refill hopper in controlled manner to avoid segregation.
4) Record level at defined intervals.
5) Investigate fluctuations impacting tablet weight.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Hopper level maintained within range; no correlation with weight variability > ±5.0 %.
5. References: QC_SOP_352

Title: In-Process Control – Sieving Efficiency Check
1. Purpose: To verify efficiency of sieving step in removing oversized particles.
2. Scope: Milling and sieving processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Collect samples before and after sieving.
2) Perform sieve analysis using calibrated stack.
3) Compare fraction retained above target mesh.
4) Calculate removal efficiency.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Oversize fraction reduced to ≤ 2.0 %; efficiency ≥ 95.0 %.
5. References: USP <786>

Title: In-Process Control – Equipment Cleanliness Verification Before Use
1. Purpose: To ensure equipment is clean prior to batch start.
2. Scope: All manufacturing equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform visual inspection under ≥ 1000 lux.
2) Verify cleaning status label and logbook.
3) Perform swab test at critical locations if required.
4) Compare results with acceptance limits.
5) Document release for use.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No visible residue; swab results ≤ established limits; documentation complete.
5. References: QC_SOP_206, QC_SOP_203

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Initiation of Deviation or Non-Conformance Record
1. Purpose: To ensure timely documentation of any deviation, excursion, or unexpected outcome observed during GMP activities.
2. Scope: All QC and manufacturing operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify and immediately record the event (deviation/OOS/atypical result) in the quality system.
2) Classify severity (minor/major/critical) based on impact.
3) Notify QA within 24 hours for significant events.
4) Assign investigation owner and define timeline.
5) Document initial description including time, location, and affected batch.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Record initiated within 1 business day; classification justified; all required fields completed.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_010

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Initial Assessment and Impact Evaluation
1. Purpose: To assess impact of a deviation or out-of-specification result on product quality and compliance.
2. Scope: All deviation and OOS investigations.
3. Procedure:
1) Review event details, batch records, and analytical data.
2) Determine potential impact on product quality, safety, and data integrity.
3) Identify affected batches and materials.
4) Decide on product disposition (e.g., quarantine).
5) Document assessment.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Assessment completed within 3 days; impact clearly justified; QA approval obtained.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Root Cause Analysis Using 5 Whys
1. Purpose: To identify root cause of a deviation or unexpected outcome.
2. Scope: All investigations requiring causal analysis.
3. Procedure:
1) Define problem statement clearly.
2) Apply 5 Whys method to trace causal factors.
3) Identify contributing factors and system weaknesses.
4) Verify root cause with evidence.
5) Document findings.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Root cause supported by data; no unresolved gaps; QA approval obtained.
5. References: QC_SOP_010

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Fishbone (Ishikawa) Analysis
1. Purpose: To systematically identify contributing factors to a non-conformance.
2. Scope: Complex investigations.
3. Procedure:
1) Define problem.
2) Categorize potential causes (Man, Machine, Method, Material, Environment).
3) Brainstorm contributing factors.
4) Evaluate likelihood.
5) Document analysis.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All relevant factors considered; analysis documented.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Laboratory OOS Investigation Procedure
1. Purpose: To investigate out-of-specification (OOS) results in laboratory testing.
2. Scope: All QC analytical testing.
3. Procedure:
1) Confirm OOS result by review of raw data.
2) Perform hypothesis testing (analyst error, instrument failure).
3) Re-test if justified.
4) Evaluate manufacturing impact.
5) Document investigation.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Investigation completed within 30 days; conclusions scientifically justified.
5. References: FDA OOS Guidance

Title: Deviation & CAPA – CAPA Plan Development
1. Purpose: To define corrective and preventive actions addressing root cause.
2. Scope: All confirmed deviations.
3. Procedure:
1) Define corrective action to eliminate root cause.
2) Define preventive action to avoid recurrence.
3) Assign responsibilities and timelines.
4) Document CAPA plan.
5) Obtain QA approval.
4. Acceptance Criteria: CAPA plan addresses root cause; timelines defined; approved before implementation.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – CAPA Implementation and Tracking
1. Purpose: To ensure CAPA actions are implemented and tracked.
2. Scope: All CAPA records.
3. Procedure:
1) Execute defined actions.
2) Track progress in system.
3) Update status regularly.
4) Verify completion.
5) Document evidence.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % actions completed within timeline; evidence documented.
5. References: QC_SOP_406

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Effectiveness Check of CAPA
1. Purpose: To verify effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions.
2. Scope: All closed CAPA.
3. Procedure:
1) Define effectiveness criteria.
2) Monitor relevant metrics.
3) Perform follow-up checks.
4) Evaluate recurrence.
5) Document outcome.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No recurrence within defined period; criteria met.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Trending of Deviations and Excursions
1. Purpose: To identify recurring issues and trends.
2. Scope: All deviation records.
3. Procedure:
1) Compile deviation data.
2) Categorize by type and root cause.
3) Perform trend analysis.
4) Identify patterns.
5) Report findings.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Trends reviewed quarterly; actions defined for recurring issues.
5. References: QC_SOP_182

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Closure of Deviation Records
1. Purpose: To ensure proper closure of investigations.
2. Scope: All deviation records.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify root cause identified.
2) Confirm CAPA implemented.
3) Review documentation.
4) Approve closure.
5) Archive record.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No open actions; QA approval obtained.
5. References: QC_SOP_010

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Escalation of Critical Excursions
1. Purpose: To ensure timely escalation of critical deviations, excursions, or non-conformances that may impact product quality or patient safety.
2. Scope: All GMP activities across QC and manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Classify event as critical based on predefined criteria (e.g., sterility breach, confirmed OOS).
2) Notify QA, QP, and site leadership within 24 hours.
3) Quarantine affected materials and halt related operations if necessary.
4) Initiate formal investigation and assign cross-functional team.
5) Document escalation and interim controls.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Escalation within 24 hours; impacted batches identified; containment actions implemented immediately.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_401

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Interim Controls for OOS and Atypical Results
1. Purpose: To define temporary controls while investigating OOS or unexpected outcomes.
2. Scope: All laboratory and manufacturing investigations.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify potential risks associated with the atypical result.
2) Implement interim controls (e.g., increased sampling, process hold, additional testing).
3) Communicate controls to relevant teams.
4) Monitor effectiveness of controls during investigation.
5) Document actions and remove controls after resolution.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Controls implemented within 2 days; no further impact observed; removal justified post-investigation.
5. References: FDA OOS Guidance, QC_SOP_402

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Human Error Assessment Framework
1. Purpose: To evaluate whether human error is a root cause or contributing factor without bias.
2. Scope: All deviation and non-conformance investigations.
3. Procedure:
1) Review training records and SOP clarity.
2) Assess workload, environment, and system design factors.
3) Determine if error was isolated or systemic.
4) Avoid assigning blame without supporting evidence.
5) Document findings and link to CAPA if required.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Root cause supported by evidence; systemic factors considered; no unjustified blame attribution.
5. References: ICH Q10, QC_SOP_403

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Equipment-Related Investigation
1. Purpose: To investigate deviations linked to equipment malfunction or variability.
2. Scope: All equipment-related excursions and failures.
3. Procedure:
1) Review equipment logs, calibration, and maintenance records.
2) Verify alarm history and sensor data.
3) Perform functional checks or requalification if needed.
4) Identify causal factors (e.g., drift, wear).
5) Document conclusions and remediation actions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Root cause identified; equipment restored to qualified state; no recurring issues.
5. References: QC_SOP_256, QC_SOP_260

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Laboratory Error Investigation (Phase I/II)
1. Purpose: To systematically investigate potential laboratory errors leading to OOS results.
2. Scope: All QC analytical testing.
3. Procedure:
1) Phase I: Review analyst technique, calculations, and instrument performance.
2) Phase II: Expand investigation to method suitability and sample integrity.
3) Evaluate re-test or re-sample justification.
4) Document findings and conclusions.
5) Escalate if no assignable cause found.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Investigation completed within 30 days; conclusions scientifically justified; QA approval obtained.
5. References: FDA OOS Guidance

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Risk Assessment Using FMEA
1. Purpose: To assess risk associated with deviations and prioritize CAPA actions.
2. Scope: All significant deviations and excursions.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify failure modes and potential effects.
2) Assign severity, occurrence, and detection scores.
3) Calculate Risk Priority Number (RPN).
4) Prioritize actions based on RPN.
5) Document assessment.
4. Acceptance Criteria: RPN thresholds defined; high-risk items addressed first; assessment approved.
5. References: ICH Q9

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Documentation Standards for Investigations
1. Purpose: To ensure consistency and completeness of investigation records.
2. Scope: All deviation, OOS, and non-conformance reports.
3. Procedure:
1) Use standardized templates.
2) Include description, root cause, impact, and CAPA.
3) Ensure traceability to batch and data.
4) Review for completeness and clarity.
5) Archive records.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No missing sections; clear and traceable documentation; QA approval obtained.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Cross-Functional Investigation Process
1. Purpose: To ensure comprehensive investigation involving all relevant functions.
2. Scope: Complex deviations and systemic issues.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify required departments (QC, QA, Production, Engineering).
2) Conduct investigation meetings.
3) Share data and findings.
4) Agree on root cause and CAPA.
5) Document outcomes.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All stakeholders involved; consensus on root cause; actions assigned.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Timeline Management for Investigations
1. Purpose: To ensure timely completion of deviation investigations.
2. Scope: All investigations.
3. Procedure:
1) Define investigation timeline (e.g., 30 days).
2) Track progress in quality system.
3) Escalate delays.
4) Extend timeline with justification if needed.
5) Document closure.
4. Acceptance Criteria: ≥ 90 % investigations closed within timeline; delays justified.
5. References: QC_SOP_401

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Linkage Between Deviation and Change Control
1. Purpose: To ensure systemic fixes are implemented through change control.
2. Scope: Deviations requiring process or system changes.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify need for change based on root cause.
2) Initiate change control.
3) Link deviation record to change request.
4) Implement and verify change.
5) Document linkage.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All systemic changes tracked; linkage documented; QA approval obtained.
5. References: QC_SOP_099

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Trending of Root Causes and Contributing Factors
1. Purpose: To identify recurring causal patterns across deviations.
2. Scope: All closed investigations.
3. Procedure:
1) Compile root cause data.
2) Categorize by type (human, equipment, method).
3) Analyze frequency and trends.
4) Identify systemic issues.
5) Recommend improvements.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Trends reviewed quarterly; actions defined for recurring causes.
5. References: QC_SOP_409

Title: Deviation & CAPA – CAPA Effectiveness Metrics Definition
1. Purpose: To define measurable criteria for CAPA effectiveness.
2. Scope: All CAPA plans.
3. Procedure:
1) Define KPIs (e.g., recurrence rate, defect reduction).
2) Set monitoring period (e.g., 3–6 months).
3) Collect and analyze data.
4) Evaluate against targets.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: KPIs achieved; no recurrence; documented evidence.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Management Review of Quality Events
1. Purpose: To provide oversight of deviations and CAPA at management level.
2. Scope: All quality events.
3. Procedure:
1) Compile summary of deviations and CAPA.
2) Present trends and risks.
3) Review effectiveness of actions.
4) Define strategic improvements.
5) Document meeting minutes.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Review conducted quarterly; actions assigned; follow-up tracked.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Investigation of Environmental Monitoring Excursions
1. Purpose: To assess EM excursions and their impact on product quality.
2. Scope: All EM-related deviations.
3. Procedure:
1) Confirm excursion result.
2) Identify organism and location.
3) Review recent activities and cleaning records.
4) Assess impact on batches.
5) Implement CAPA.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Investigation completed within 30 days; no product impact or justified.
5. References: EU Annex 1

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Closure Documentation and Archiving
1. Purpose: To ensure proper documentation and archiving of closed investigations.
2. Scope: All deviation and CAPA records.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify all sections completed.
2) Confirm CAPA implemented and effective.
3) Obtain QA approval.
4) Archive in quality system.
5) Ensure retrievability.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Complete records; QA approval; retrievable within 24 hours.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Hypothesis-Driven Investigation for Atypical Results
1. Purpose: To structure investigations of atypical results using testable hypotheses and evidence-based elimination.
2. Scope: All OOS, atypical results, and unexpected outcomes in QC and manufacturing.
3. Procedure:
1) Define clear problem statement and generate ≥3 plausible hypotheses (method, material, equipment).
2) Design targeted tests (e.g., system suitability recheck, sample re-prep, instrument check).
3) Execute tests with controls and document outcomes.
4) Eliminate/confirm hypotheses based on data.
5) Conclude root cause and document supporting evidence.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Hypotheses tested with data; root cause supported by evidence; no unjustified conclusions.
5. References: FDA OOS Guidance, QC_SOP_403

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Contributing Factor Analysis Using Barrier Model
1. Purpose: To identify contributing factors and failed barriers leading to non-conformance.
2. Scope: All major/critical deviations and excursions.
3. Procedure:
1) Map process steps and existing controls (barriers).
2) Identify where barriers failed or were absent.
3) Classify contributing factors (human, equipment, method, environment).
4) Propose remediation to strengthen barriers.
5) Document analysis and linkage to CAPA.
4. Acceptance Criteria: At least one failed barrier identified; contributing factors categorized; CAPA addresses barrier gaps.
5. References: ICH Q9, QC_SOP_404

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Data Integrity Assessment in Investigations
1. Purpose: To assess potential data integrity issues associated with deviations or OOS results.
2. Scope: All investigations involving electronic or paper data.
3. Procedure:
1) Review audit trails for creation, modification, and deletion events.
2) Verify ALCOA+ attributes (Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate).
3) Cross-check raw data with reported results.
4) Identify any unauthorized changes or gaps.
5) Document findings and escalate if integrity breach suspected.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No unexplained audit trail events; full traceability; any gaps investigated within 5 days.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 11, GAMP 5

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Sampling and Re-Sampling Justification
1. Purpose: To define criteria for re-sampling following an OOS or atypical result.
2. Scope: All laboratory investigations.
3. Procedure:
1) Evaluate original sampling integrity and representativeness.
2) Justify re-sampling based on documented assignable cause (e.g., sampling error).
3) Define re-sampling plan (locations, quantities).
4) Execute sampling under controlled conditions.
5) Compare results with original data and conclude.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Re-sampling justified with documented cause; results consistent with investigation outcome; QA approval.
5. References: FDA OOS Guidance

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Re-Test Policy for Out-of-Specification Results
1. Purpose: To control re-testing practices to avoid data bias.
2. Scope: All QC analytical testing.
3. Procedure:
1) Allow re-test only with documented, scientifically justified cause.
2) Define number of re-tests (e.g., maximum of 2) in protocol.
3) Use same sample preparation where applicable.
4) Evaluate all results (original and re-test) in final conclusion.
5) Document decision rationale.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No unjustified re-testing; full data set considered; compliance with SOP.
5. References: FDA OOS Guidance, QC_SOP_405

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Batch Impact Assessment for Excursions
1. Purpose: To evaluate impact of deviations/excursions on batch quality and disposition.
2. Scope: All batches associated with deviations.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify affected batches and processing stages.
2) Review critical quality attributes and IPC data.
3) Perform additional testing if required.
4) Assess risk to product quality and patient safety.
5) Recommend disposition (release, reject, rework).
4. Acceptance Criteria: Assessment completed within 5 days; decision justified with data; QA/QP approval obtained.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Effectiveness Verification Using Statistical Monitoring
1. Purpose: To confirm CAPA effectiveness using statistical process control (SPC).
2. Scope: All implemented CAPA actions.
3. Procedure:
1) Define control charts (e.g., X-bar/R) for relevant metrics.
2) Collect data over defined period (e.g., 3 months).
3) Analyze for shifts, trends, and outliers.
4) Compare pre- and post-CAPA performance.
5) Document effectiveness conclusion.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No special-cause variation; metric improvement ≥ 20.0 % where applicable; no recurrence.
5. References: ICH Q10, QC_SOP_408

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Training Effectiveness Assessment as Preventive Action
1. Purpose: To verify that training-based CAPA reduces recurrence of human-factor issues.
2. Scope: CAPA involving SOP revisions and personnel training.
3. Procedure:
1) Deliver targeted training and record attendance.
2) Conduct post-training assessment (≥10 questions) within 7 days.
3) Monitor related deviation rates for 3 months.
4) Interview operators for comprehension gaps.
5) Document outcomes and adjust training if needed.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Assessment score ≥ 85.0 %; related deviations reduced by ≥ 30.0 %; no repeat of same error.
5. References: QC_SOP_233, ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Supplier-Related Non-Conformance Investigation
1. Purpose: To investigate deviations linked to incoming materials or supplier performance.
2. Scope: All supplier-related excursions and OOS results.
3. Procedure:
1) Review CoA versus internal test results (QC_SOP_319).
2) Evaluate supplier history and recent changes.
3) Initiate supplier notification and request investigation.
4) Perform confirmatory testing (identity/assay/impurities).
5) Define CAPA including supplier qualification updates.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Root cause identified or supplier CAPA received within 30 days; material disposition justified.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_301

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Environmental Monitoring (EM) Atypical Trend Investigation
1. Purpose: To investigate atypical EM trends not exceeding action limits but indicating potential risk.
2. Scope: Viable/non-viable EM data in classified areas.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify upward trends versus historical baseline.
2) Review cleaning, personnel flow, and recent maintenance.
3) Increase sampling frequency at affected sites.
4) Identify organisms for trend correlation.
5) Implement preventive actions and document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Trend reversed within next 3 monitoring events; no action limit breaches; documentation complete.
5. References: EU Annex 1, QC_SOP_171

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Documentation of Interim Risk Mitigation
1. Purpose: To record interim remediation actions during ongoing investigations.
2. Scope: All active deviation/CAPA records.
3. Procedure:
1) Define interim controls (e.g., line hold, enhanced IPC, additional cleaning).
2) Assign responsibilities and start dates.
3) Monitor effectiveness daily/shift-wise.
4) Record outcomes and adjustments.
5) Remove controls upon final resolution with justification.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Interim controls documented within 24 hours; effectiveness demonstrated; removal approved by QA.
5. References: QC_SOP_412

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Multi-Batch Trend Analysis for Recurring Issues
1. Purpose: To detect recurrence across batches indicating systemic non-conformance.
2. Scope: All products with ≥3 similar deviations within 6 months.
3. Procedure:
1) Aggregate deviation records and categorize by root cause.
2) Analyze frequency, severity, and timing across batches.
3) Identify common causal factors.
4) Propose systemic CAPA (process redesign, control enhancement).
5) Document analysis and management approval.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Root cause recurrence rate reduced by ≥ 50.0 % post-CAPA; analysis completed within 15 days.
5. References: QC_SOP_409, ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Independent QA Review and Challenge
1. Purpose: To ensure objective evaluation of investigation conclusions and CAPA.
2. Scope: All major/critical deviations and OOS cases.
3. Procedure:
1) QA reviewer independently assesses data, rationale, and conclusions.
2) Challenge assumptions and request additional evidence if needed.
3) Verify alignment with procedures and regulations.
4) Approve or reject investigation with comments.
5) Document review outcomes.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All critical investigations undergo QA review; no unresolved QA comments at closure.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Electronic Workflow and Audit Trail Management
1. Purpose: To manage deviation/CAPA workflows within electronic QMS ensuring traceability.
2. Scope: All electronic records for deviations and CAPA.
3. Procedure:
1) Create records with unique identifiers and role-based access.
2) Capture all status changes with timestamps in audit trail.
3) Route for review/approval per workflow.
4) Lock records upon closure.
5) Periodically review audit trails for anomalies.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % actions traceable; no unauthorized edits; audit trail review completed quarterly.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Final Disposition Decision and QP Certification
1. Purpose: To formalize batch disposition following investigation and CAPA completion.
2. Scope: All impacted batches subject to deviation or OOS.
3. Procedure:
1) Compile investigation report, impact assessment, and CAPA evidence.
2) Review all analytical and IPC data for the batch.
3) Recommend disposition (release/reject/rework) with justification.
4) Obtain QA and QP approval/certification where applicable.
5) Document final decision and archive.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Decision supported by complete data; QP certification completed where required; records retrievable within 24 hours.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Cross-Site Signal Detection and Escalation
1. Purpose: To identify recurring deviations, excursions, or OOS signals across multiple sites and escalate systemic risks.
2. Scope: All quality events across global manufacturing sites.
3. Procedure:
1) Aggregate deviation and CAPA data from all sites monthly.
2) Normalize categories (OOS, non-conformance, atypical result) for comparability.
3) Perform trend analysis and identify recurring causal factors.
4) Escalate significant signals to global QA governance.
5) Define global remediation actions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Signals identified within 30 days; escalation documented; corrective actions implemented globally.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Investigation of Process Drift and Gradual Excursions
1. Purpose: To identify slow process drift leading to atypical results without immediate OOS.
2. Scope: Continuous and batch processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Analyze historical IPC and EM data for trends.
2) Identify gradual shifts in key parameters.
3) Correlate drift with process variables.
4) Define root cause and contributing factors.
5) Implement preventive actions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Drift identified before OOS occurrence; parameter variation controlled within ±5.0 %.
5. References: QC_SOP_409

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Investigation Closure Quality Review Checklist
1. Purpose: To ensure completeness and robustness of investigation reports before closure.
2. Scope: All deviation and CAPA records.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify root cause clearly defined and supported by data.
2) Confirm contributing factors evaluated.
3) Check CAPA adequacy and linkage.
4) Ensure all sections completed.
5) Document QA review outcome.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % checklist completion; no missing justification; QA approval required.
5. References: QC_SOP_417

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Recurrent Deviation Escalation Process
1. Purpose: To escalate repeated non-conformances indicating systemic failure.
2. Scope: Deviations recurring ≥3 times in 6 months.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify recurrence using trending tools.
2) Perform comprehensive root cause re-evaluation.
3) Escalate to management review board.
4) Define enhanced CAPA strategy.
5) Document escalation and decisions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Escalation within 5 days of detection; recurrence reduced ≥50 % post-CAPA.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Investigation of Data Outliers and Statistical Anomalies
1. Purpose: To assess unexpected outcomes detected through statistical analysis.
2. Scope: QC analytical and IPC datasets.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify outliers using statistical tests (e.g., Grubbs test).
2) Review raw data and instrument logs.
3) Assess assignable cause.
4) Confirm or reject outlier status.
5) Document decision.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Outlier justified or included in dataset; statistical method documented.
5. References: ICH Q2(R2)

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Supplier CAPA Follow-Up and Verification
1. Purpose: To ensure supplier corrective actions are effective.
2. Scope: Supplier-related deviations.
3. Procedure:
1) Review supplier CAPA documentation.
2) Verify implementation evidence.
3) Perform incoming material testing for confirmation.
4) Monitor future lots.
5) Document closure.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Supplier CAPA effective; no recurrence in ≥3 subsequent lots.
5. References: QC_SOP_434

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Documentation of Root Cause vs Contributing Factors
1. Purpose: To clearly distinguish primary root cause from contributing factors.
2. Scope: All investigations.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify all potential causes.
2) Evaluate causal relationships.
3) Define primary root cause.
4) List contributing factors.
5) Document clearly.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Clear distinction documented; supported by evidence.
5. References: QC_SOP_403

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Audit Trail Review During Investigations
1. Purpose: To verify data integrity during deviation analysis.
2. Scope: All electronic systems.
3. Procedure:
1) Extract audit trail data.
2) Review for anomalies.
3) Compare with reported data.
4) Identify unauthorized changes.
5) Document findings.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No unexplained modifications; audit trail complete.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Risk-Based Prioritization of CAPA Actions
1. Purpose: To prioritize corrective actions based on risk.
2. Scope: All CAPA plans.
3. Procedure:
1) Assess severity, occurrence, and detectability.
2) Calculate risk score.
3) Rank CAPA actions.
4) Implement high-priority actions first.
5) Document prioritization.
4. Acceptance Criteria: High-risk CAPA addressed within defined timeline; prioritization justified.
5. References: ICH Q9

Title: Deviation & CAPA – Final CAPA Closure and Knowledge Management
1. Purpose: To ensure CAPA outcomes are captured and shared for continuous improvement.
2. Scope: All completed CAPA.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify CAPA effectiveness.
2) Document lessons learned.
3) Update SOPs or training materials.
4) Share knowledge across departments.
5) Archive CAPA record.
4. Acceptance Criteria: CAPA closed with documented effectiveness; knowledge shared; no recurrence.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Change Control – Initiation of Change Request
1. Purpose: To formally initiate and document changes to GMP systems, processes, or documents.
2. Scope: All changes impacting quality systems.
3. Procedure:
1) Submit change request with description and rationale.
2) Assign change category and priority.
3) Route for initial QA review.
4) Record impacted systems.
5) Document request.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Request complete; QA review initiated within 2 days.
5. References: QC_SOP_099

Title: Change Control – Impact Assessment and Risk Evaluation
1. Purpose: To assess impact of proposed change on product quality.
2. Scope: All change requests.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify affected processes and systems.
2) Perform risk assessment (FMEA).
3) Evaluate regulatory impact.
4) Define mitigation actions.
5) Document assessment.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Risk assessed; mitigation defined; QA approval obtained.
5. References: ICH Q9

Title: Change Control – Approval Workflow Management
1. Purpose: To ensure proper approval of changes.
2. Scope: All change controls.
3. Procedure:
1) Route change for approval (QA, QC, Production).
2) Review documentation.
3) Approve or reject.
4) Record decisions.
5) Archive.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All approvals obtained; no unauthorized implementation.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Change Control – Implementation of Approved Changes
1. Purpose: To ensure controlled execution of approved changes.
2. Scope: All approved changes.
3. Procedure:
1) Execute change per plan.
2) Update SOPs and systems.
3) Train personnel.
4) Verify implementation.
5) Document completion.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Change implemented as approved; training completed.
5. References: QC_SOP_099

Title: Change Control – Verification and Closure of Changes
1. Purpose: To confirm effectiveness of implemented changes.
2. Scope: All completed changes.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify outcomes against objectives.
2) Review data and performance.
3) Confirm no adverse impact.
4) Approve closure.
5) Archive.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Objectives met; no unintended consequences.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Change Control – Classification of Change Types
1. Purpose: To categorize changes (minor, major, critical) based on potential impact to product quality and compliance.
2. Scope: All change control requests within GMP systems.
3. Procedure:
1) Review proposed change description and affected systems.
2) Assess impact on validated state, regulatory filings, and product quality.
3) Classify change as minor, major, or critical using predefined criteria.
4) Document rationale for classification.
5) Route to appropriate approval pathway based on classification.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Classification justified and documented; QA approval obtained prior to further processing.
5. References: ICH Q10, QC_SOP_451

Title: Change Control – Regulatory Impact Assessment
1. Purpose: To evaluate whether a proposed change requires regulatory notification or approval.
2. Scope: All changes affecting registered products or filings.
3. Procedure:
1) Review current regulatory filings (e.g., NDA, MA) for impacted sections.
2) Determine change category per regional guidelines (e.g., prior approval, notification).
3) Consult regulatory affairs for classification.
4) Document submission requirements and timelines.
5) Ensure approval obtained before implementation where required.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Regulatory classification documented; submissions completed before implementation if required.
5. References: ICH Q10, regional regulatory guidelines

Title: Change Control – Validation Impact Assessment
1. Purpose: To determine validation or requalification requirements resulting from a change.
2. Scope: All changes affecting equipment, processes, or analytical methods.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify impacted validated systems (process, cleaning, analytical).
2) Assess extent of revalidation (partial or full).
3) Define validation plan and acceptance criteria.
4) Execute validation activities.
5) Document outcomes and update validation status.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Validation activities completed prior to release; results meet acceptance criteria.
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_254

Title: Change Control – Documentation Update and Version Control
1. Purpose: To ensure controlled update of SOPs and documents following changes.
2. Scope: All GMP documentation affected by change control.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify documents requiring revision.
2) Update content with tracked changes and new revision number.
3) Route for review and approval.
4) Implement version control and archive superseded versions.
5) Distribute updated documents to users.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Correct version implemented; obsolete versions removed; audit trail maintained.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_032

Title: Change Control – Training Following Change Implementation
1. Purpose: To ensure personnel are trained on updated processes or documents.
2. Scope: All employees impacted by changes.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify affected personnel.
2) Develop training materials reflecting changes.
3) Conduct training sessions and assessments.
4) Record attendance and competency results.
5) Verify understanding before execution of changed process.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Training completion ≥ 100 %; assessment score ≥ 85.0 %; records documented.
5. References: QC_SOP_233

Title: Change Control – Temporary Change (Deviation-Based Change)
1. Purpose: To manage temporary changes implemented via deviation or excursion.
