2. Scope: Short-term changes not intended for permanent implementation.
3. Procedure:
1) Initiate deviation describing temporary change.
2) Assess impact and define duration.
3) Implement temporary controls.
4) Monitor performance during period.
5) Revert to original state or formalize change via change control.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Temporary change duration defined; no adverse impact observed; closure documented.
5. References: QC_SOP_401

Title: Change Control – Emergency Change Management
1. Purpose: To manage urgent changes required to address critical issues.
2. Scope: All emergency situations impacting GMP operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify emergency and justify immediate action.
2) Obtain expedited QA approval.
3) Implement change with minimal delay.
4) Document actions retrospectively.
5) Conduct full impact assessment post-implementation.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Emergency justified; documentation completed within 5 days; no uncontrolled impact.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Change Control – Change Effectiveness Verification
1. Purpose: To confirm that implemented changes achieve intended outcomes.
2. Scope: All closed change controls.
3. Procedure:
1) Define effectiveness criteria (e.g., reduced deviation rate).
2) Monitor process performance over defined period.
3) Compare pre- and post-change data.
4) Document evaluation.
5) Approve effectiveness.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Objectives met; no negative trends; QA approval obtained.
5. References: QC_SOP_455

Title: Change Control – Change Log and Tracking System
1. Purpose: To maintain centralized tracking of all change control records.
2. Scope: All change requests.
3. Procedure:
1) Assign unique change ID.
2) Record status updates.
3) Monitor timelines and approvals.
4) Generate periodic reports.
5) Archive closed changes.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100 % traceability; no overdue changes; data updated within 24 hours.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Change Control – Risk-Based Change Prioritization
1. Purpose: To prioritize changes based on risk to product quality.
2. Scope: All change control requests.
3. Procedure:
1) Assess risk using severity, occurrence, detectability.
2) Assign priority level.
3) Schedule implementation accordingly.
4) Monitor high-risk changes closely.
5) Document prioritization.
4. Acceptance Criteria: High-risk changes prioritized; rationale documented.
5. References: ICH Q9

Title: Change Control – Supplier Change Notification Management
1. Purpose: To manage changes initiated by suppliers.
2. Scope: All supplier-related changes.
3. Procedure:
1) Receive supplier notification.
2) Assess impact on product quality.
3) Initiate internal change control.
4) Perform additional testing if required.
5) Approve or reject change.
4. Acceptance Criteria: All supplier changes assessed; no unapproved changes implemented.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Change Control – Change Implementation Timeline Management
1. Purpose: To ensure timely execution of approved changes.
2. Scope: All change controls.
3. Procedure:
1) Define timeline.
2) Track progress.
3) Escalate delays.
4) Update status.
5) Document completion.
4. Acceptance Criteria: ≥ 90 % changes completed within timeline.
5. References: QC_SOP_419

Title: Change Control – Post-Implementation Review
1. Purpose: To evaluate impact of implemented change.
2. Scope: All completed changes.
3. Procedure:
1) Review process performance.
2) Identify unintended effects.
3) Document findings.
4) Implement corrective actions if needed.
5) Close review.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No adverse impact; review completed within 30 days.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Change Control – Documentation of Change History
1. Purpose: To maintain historical record of changes.
2. Scope: All GMP systems.
3. Procedure:
1) Record change details.
2) Maintain version history.
3) Ensure traceability.
4) Archive records.
5) Retrieve when needed.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Complete history available; retrievable within 24 hours.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Change Control – Final Change Closure and Archiving
1. Purpose: To ensure proper closure and archival of change records.
2. Scope: All completed change controls.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify all actions completed.
2) Confirm effectiveness.
3) Obtain QA approval.
4) Archive record.
5) Ensure retrievability.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No open actions; QA approval; records retrievable.
5. References: QC_SOP_455

Title: Change Control – Periodic Review of Open Changes
1. Purpose: To ensure timely progression and oversight of open change controls.
2. Scope: All active change control records.
3. Procedure:
1) Generate weekly report of open changes from QMS.
2) Review aging (e.g., >30, >60 days) and identify bottlenecks.
3) Contact owners to update status and remove blockers.
4) Escalate overdue critical changes to QA management.
5) Document review outcomes and actions taken.
4. Acceptance Criteria: ≥ 90.0 % of changes within timeline; all critical changes reviewed weekly; overdue items have documented action plans.
5. References: QC_SOP_464, QC_SOP_467

Title: Change Control – Data Migration and System Change Verification
1. Purpose: To verify integrity and completeness of data during system changes or migrations.
2. Scope: All computerized systems subject to change or upgrade.
3. Procedure:
1) Define data sets and migration mapping.
2) Perform test migration in validation environment.
3) Verify record counts, checksums, and critical fields.
4) Execute user acceptance testing (UAT).
5) Document discrepancies and finalize go-live approval.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100.0 % record reconciliation; no critical data loss; UAT pass rate ≥ 95.0 %.
5. References: GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Change Control – Configuration Change to Analytical Methods (HPLC/GC)
1. Purpose: To control changes to analytical method parameters ensuring validated performance.
2. Scope: HPLC and GC methods used in QC.
3. Procedure:
1) Propose change (e.g., column type, flow rate, gradient).
2) Assess impact on validation characteristics (accuracy, precision, robustness).
3) Execute bridging study with system suitability and comparative analysis.
4) Update method SOP and CDS parameters.
5) Train analysts and document implementation.
4. Acceptance Criteria: System suitability met (e.g., resolution ≥ 2.0, %RSD ≤ 2.0 %); no bias > ±2.0 % vs original method.
5. References: USP <621>, ICH Q2(R2)

Title: Change Control – Packaging Component Artwork Revision
1. Purpose: To manage controlled updates to labeling and artwork to prevent mislabeling.
2. Scope: Labels, cartons, and leaflets.
3. Procedure:
1) Initiate change with revised artwork and justification.
2) Perform regulatory/medical review of content.
3) Verify barcode (EAN/GS1) and print quality specifications.
4) Conduct line trial and readability checks.
5) Approve and release new version; obsolete old stock per procedure.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 0 labeling errors in trial; barcode readability grade ≥ C; 100.0 % obsolete stock disposition documented.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Change Control – Cleaning Process Change Assessment
1. Purpose: To evaluate impact of changes to cleaning agents, cycles, or limits.
2. Scope: Equipment cleaning processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify proposed change (detergent, concentration, cycle time).
2) Assess impact on residue limits (MACO) and sampling methods.
3) Perform cleaning verification/validation (swab/rinse) under worst-case.
4) Analyze residues via validated methods (e.g., TOC/HPLC).
5) Update SOPs and train operators.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residues ≤ established limits; recovery 70.0–130.0 %; no carryover detected.
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_206

Title: Change Control – Environmental Monitoring Program Update
1. Purpose: To manage changes to EM locations, frequencies, or limits.
2. Scope: Viable and non-viable monitoring programs.
3. Procedure:
1) Propose change based on trend analysis or facility modification.
2) Assess impact on contamination control strategy.
3) Perform qualification (e.g., location justification, smoke studies if needed).
4) Update EM SOPs and sampling plans.
5) Train personnel and implement.
4. Acceptance Criteria: New program meets ISO/EU Annex 1 limits; no increase in action-level breaches post-change.
5. References: EU Annex 1, QC_SOP_171

Title: Change Control – Supplier Change Evaluation (Material Specification)
1. Purpose: To assess impact of supplier-initiated changes to material specifications.
2. Scope: APIs and critical excipients.
3. Procedure:
1) Review supplier change notice (spec limits, process changes).
2) Compare with internal specifications and validated ranges.
3) Perform confirmatory testing (identity, assay, impurities).
4) Update specifications or reject change.
5) Document decision and notify stakeholders.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Material meets internal specs; no adverse impact on product CQAs; approval documented.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211, QC_SOP_466

Title: Change Control – Equipment Relocation/Reinstallation
1. Purpose: To control risks associated with relocating qualified equipment.
2. Scope: Movement of QC or manufacturing equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Initiate change and define new location requirements (utilities, space).
2) Perform deinstallation and transport under controlled conditions.
3) Reinstall and execute IQ/OQ (and PQ if required).
4) Verify calibration and system suitability.
5) Release equipment for use upon QA approval.
4. Acceptance Criteria: IQ/OQ acceptance met; system suitability within limits; no performance degradation observed.
5. References: EU Annex 15, QC_SOP_254

Title: Change Control – Computerized System Patch/Upgrade Management
1. Purpose: To manage patches/upgrades without compromising validated state.
2. Scope: LIMS, ELN, CDS, and SCADA systems.
3. Procedure:
1) Review vendor release notes and impact.
2) Assess GxP impact and define test scope.
3) Execute regression testing in validation environment.
4) Schedule controlled deployment and backup.
5) Verify post-installation functionality and audit trails.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100.0 % critical tests passed; no audit trail anomalies; system uptime ≥ 99.0 % post-change.
5. References: GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11

Title: Change Control – Change Communication and Stakeholder Notification
1. Purpose: To ensure all impacted stakeholders are informed of changes.
2. Scope: All approved changes affecting operations.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify impacted departments (QC, QA, Production, Engineering).
2) Prepare change summary and effective date.
3) Distribute communication via controlled channels.
4) Confirm receipt and understanding.
5) Record communication evidence.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100.0 % stakeholder notification; acknowledgments recorded; no execution prior to effective date.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Change Control – KPI Monitoring for Change Management
1. Purpose: To monitor performance of the change control system.
2. Scope: All change records.
3. Procedure:
1) Define KPIs (on-time closure, rework rate, effectiveness).
2) Extract monthly data from QMS.
3) Analyze trends and identify gaps.
4) Present results in management review.
5) Define improvement actions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: On-time closure ≥ 90.0 %; rework rate ≤ 5.0 %; effectiveness pass rate ≥ 95.0 %.
5. References: QC_SOP_423

Title: Change Control – Linkage to Deviation/CAPA for Systemic Fixes
1. Purpose: To ensure systemic issues identified in deviations are resolved via formal changes.
2. Scope: Changes arising from deviation/CAPA investigations.
3. Procedure:
1) Review investigation root cause and recommended actions.
2) Initiate linked change control with cross-reference IDs.
3) Define scope (process, equipment, document).
4) Implement and verify changes.
5) Close both records with documented linkage.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100.0 % linkage documented; change addresses root cause; effectiveness verified.
5. References: QC_SOP_420

Title: Change Control – Validation Documentation Update (Protocols/Reports)
1. Purpose: To ensure validation documents reflect implemented changes.
2. Scope: Process, cleaning, and analytical validation documents.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify affected protocols/reports.
2) Revise acceptance criteria or methods as needed.
3) Route for QA approval with revision control.
4) Archive superseded versions.
5) Distribute updated documents.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Correct version in use; revision history complete; QA approval documented.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Change Control – Post-Implementation Audit
1. Purpose: To verify compliance after change implementation.
2. Scope: Major and critical changes.
3. Procedure:
1) Schedule audit within 30–60 days post-implementation.
2) Review adherence to updated SOPs and records.
3) Interview personnel for process understanding.
4) Identify gaps or non-conformances.
5) Document findings and initiate CAPA if required.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No critical findings; minor findings addressed within 30 days; audit report approved.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Change Control – Final Compilation and Archival of Change Dossier
1. Purpose: To compile complete change dossier for audit readiness and knowledge retention.
2. Scope: All closed change controls.
3. Procedure:
1) Assemble request, impact assessment, approvals, validation, and training records.
2) Verify completeness against checklist.
3) Convert to controlled archive format with indexing.
4) Store in electronic repository with access control.
5) Ensure retrievability for inspections.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100.0 % documents present; indexed and retrievable within 24 hours; audit trail intact.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 11, QC_SOP_470

Title: Change Control – Change Freeze and Release Management
1. Purpose: To control implementation of changes during critical manufacturing or regulatory periods.
2. Scope: All GMP systems during defined freeze periods (e.g., validation campaigns, inspections).
3. Procedure:
1) Define change freeze window and communicate to stakeholders.
2) Review pending changes and defer non-critical items.
3) Allow only emergency changes with QA approval.
4) Track all changes implemented during freeze.
5) Release freeze after review and approval.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100.0 % compliance with freeze; only approved emergency changes executed; full traceability maintained.
5. References: ICH Q10, QC_SOP_462

Title: Change Control – Validation Master Plan (VMP) Update Following Change
1. Purpose: To ensure VMP reflects current validated state after significant changes.
2. Scope: All major and critical changes impacting validation scope.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify sections of VMP impacted by change.
2) Update validation strategy and scope.
3) Align qualification and validation schedules.
4) Route updated VMP for QA approval.
5) Distribute updated version.
4. Acceptance Criteria: VMP updated within 30 days; alignment with implemented changes; QA approval documented.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Change Control – Control of Parallel Changes and Dependencies
1. Purpose: To manage multiple simultaneous changes and their interdependencies.
2. Scope: All concurrent change control records.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify related changes and dependencies.
2) Map sequence and potential conflicts.
3) Coordinate implementation timelines.
4) Monitor interactions during execution.
5) Document outcomes and adjustments.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No conflicting implementations; dependencies managed; documentation complete.
5. References: QC_SOP_464

Title: Change Control – Risk Communication to Regulatory Authorities
1. Purpose: To communicate high-risk changes impacting regulatory filings.
2. Scope: Changes requiring regulatory interaction.
3. Procedure:
1) Prepare change summary and risk assessment.
2) Draft regulatory submission or notification.
3) Submit within required timeline.
4) Address authority queries.
5) Document communication.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Submission complete and accepted; no compliance gaps.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Change Control – Control of Obsolete Materials Post-Change
1. Purpose: To prevent use of obsolete materials following specification or process changes.
2. Scope: Raw materials, packaging components, and intermediates.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify obsolete materials post-change.
2) Segregate and label as obsolete.
3) Decide disposition (rework, return, destroy).
4) Record inventory adjustments.
5) Verify removal from use.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100.0 % obsolete materials segregated; no unintended use.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Change Control – Stability Impact Assessment After Change
1. Purpose: To evaluate impact of change on product stability profile.
2. Scope: All product-related changes.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify stability-indicating attributes.
2) Initiate stability study (accelerated/long-term).
3) Monitor results over timepoints.
4) Compare with historical data.
5) Document conclusions.
4. Acceptance Criteria: No significant degradation; results within specification at all timepoints.
5. References: ICH Q1A

Title: Change Control – Analytical Method Transfer Following Change
1. Purpose: To ensure method performance at receiving site after change.
2. Scope: Analytical methods transferred between labs.
3. Procedure:
1) Define transfer protocol.
2) Perform comparative testing (sending vs receiving site).
3) Evaluate accuracy, precision, and reproducibility.
4) Document results.
5) Approve method at receiving site.
4. Acceptance Criteria: %RSD ≤ 5.0 %; results within ±2.0 % bias.
5. References: ICH Q2(R2)

Title: Change Control – Cleaning Validation Reassessment
1. Purpose: To reassess cleaning validation after process or product change.
2. Scope: Equipment cleaning processes.
3. Procedure:
1) Identify worst-case product.
2) Perform cleaning verification.
3) Analyze residues (HPLC/TOC).
4) Compare with limits.
5) Document results.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Residues ≤ established limits; recovery 70.0–130.0 %.
5. References: EU Annex 15

Title: Change Control – Packaging Line Qualification After Change
1. Purpose: To requalify packaging line after modifications.
2. Scope: Packaging equipment.
3. Procedure:
1) Perform IQ/OQ after modification.
2) Conduct trial run with product.
3) Verify labeling and sealing.
4) Record results.
5) Approve for use.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 0 defects; all parameters within limits.
5. References: QC_SOP_254

Title: Change Control – Data Review and Final Approval
1. Purpose: To ensure all data related to change is reviewed before closure.
2. Scope: All change records.
3. Procedure:
1) Compile all data.
2) Review for completeness.
3) Verify against objectives.
4) Approve.
5) Archive.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Complete data; QA approval.
5. References: QC_SOP_455

Title: Change Control – Periodic System Audit of Change Control Process
1. Purpose: To evaluate effectiveness of change control system.
2. Scope: Entire QMS change control process.
3. Procedure:
1) Plan audit schedule.
2) Review change records.
3) Identify gaps.
4) Recommend improvements.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Audit completed annually; corrective actions defined.
5. References: ICH Q10

Title: Change Control – Integration with CAPA System
1. Purpose: To ensure alignment between change control and CAPA.
2. Scope: All related systems.
3. Procedure:
1) Link change and CAPA records.
2) Track implementation.
3) Verify effectiveness.
4) Document linkage.
5) Close records.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Linkage documented; effectiveness confirmed.
5. References: QC_SOP_482

Title: Change Control – Final QA Review and Sign-Off
1. Purpose: To ensure final QA oversight before closure.
2. Scope: All change controls.
3. Procedure:
1) Review documentation.
2) Verify compliance.
3) Approve closure.
4) Archive.
5) Document.
4. Acceptance Criteria: QA approval obtained; no open actions.
5. References: 21 CFR Part 211

Title: Change Control – Change History Trending and Reporting
1. Purpose: To analyze trends in changes for continuous improvement.
2. Scope: All change records.
3. Procedure:
1) Compile change data.
2) Analyze trends.
3) Identify recurring issues.
4) Report findings.
5) Implement improvements.
4. Acceptance Criteria: Trends reviewed quarterly; actions defined.
5. References: QC_SOP_481

Title: Change Control – Final System Closure and Continuous Improvement
1. Purpose: To ensure closure of change system and capture improvements.
2. Scope: Entire change control lifecycle.
3. Procedure:
1) Verify all changes closed.
2) Review system performance.
3) Identify improvement opportunities.
4) Update procedures.
5) Document outcomes.
4. Acceptance Criteria: 100.0 % closure; continuous improvement documented.
5. References: ICH Q10
